His saying: ﴿فَأَجَآءَهَا ٱلْمَخَاضُ﴾ (and the pains of childbirth drove her): from جئت (to come), as you say: "the pains of childbirth came with her to the trunk of the palm tree". When you drop the bāʾ, you put an alif in the verb; as you say: آتيتكَ زيدا (I brought you Zayd), meaning أتيتك بزيد. Similar is ﴿آتُونِى زُبَرَ الحَدِيدِ﴾ (bring me sheets of iron): when you dropped the bāʾ you added an alif, and it is only ائتونى بزُبَر الحديد. There is another dialect form, not suitable in the Book, which is Tamīmī: فأشَاءَهَا المَخَاضُ. Among the proverbs of the Arabs: شرٌّ مَا ألجأك إلى مُخَّة عُرْقُوب (it was something bad that drove you to the marrow of a hock); the people of the Ḥijāz and the people of al-ʿĀliya say: شرّ مَا أجاءك إلى مُخَّة عرقوب, and the meaning is the same; and Tamīm say: شرّ مَا أشاءك إلى مُخَّة عرقوب.
His saying: ﴿وَكُنتُ نَسْياً﴾ (and had been a thing forgotten): [109a] «[Translator's note: "109 ا" is a manuscript folio marker.]» the companions of ʿAbdallāh read نَسْيا with fatḥa on the nūn, and the rest of the Arabs give the nūn kasra; they are two dialect forms, like الجَسْر and الجِسْر (bridge), الحَجْر and الحِجْر, and الوَتْر and الوِتْر (odd number). النِّسْى is the rags of her impurity that a woman throws away (because when it is thrown away it is not taken back); it is اللَّقَى, with the short ending. It is النَّسْى; and had you meant by النَّسْى the maṣdar (verbal noun) of forgetting, it would have been correct — like your saying: حِجْرا محجوراً, i.e. حراما محرما (wholly forbidden), and نَسْيا مَنِسيّا (utterly forgotten). The Arabs say: نسيته نِسياناً and نسيا (I forgot it). One of them recited to me:
* من طاعة الربّ وعَصْى الشيطان *
(… out of obedience to the Lord and disobedience to Satan.)
He means: وعصيان الشيطان. Likewise أتيته إتيانا and أَتْياً (I came to him). The poet said:
أَتْىُ الفواحشِ فيهمُ معروفة * ويرون فعل المكرُمات حَرَامَا
(Committing indecencies is well known among them, and they regard doing noble deeds as forbidden.)

farraa:57-57.t: His saying: ﴿وَرَفَعْنَاهُ مَكَاناً عَلِيّاً﴾: it is related that Idrīs was [Translator's note: the text has «كا», evidently for «كان»] made beloved to the Angel of Death, so that he asked his Lord's permission to take him as a close friend. Then Idrīs asked the Angel of Death to show him the Fire; so he asked his Lord's permission and showed it to him. Then (he asked his Lord's permission) regarding Paradise, and showed it to him, and he entered it. The Angel of Death said to him: "Come out." He said: "By Allah, I will never come out of it, because Allah said ﴿وَإِنْ مِنْكُمْ إلاَّ وَارِدُهَا﴾, and I have already come down to it" — meaning the Fire — "and He said ﴿وَمَا هُمْ منها بِمُخْرَجِينَ﴾, so I will not come out of it except by His permission." So Allah said: "By My permission he entered it, so leave him." That is His saying ﴿وَرَفَعْنَاه مَكَاناً عَلِيّاً﴾.

farraa:24-24.t: His saying: ﴿فَنَادَاهَا مِن تَحْتِهَآ﴾ (then he called her from beneath her) and ﴿نَادَاهَا مِن تَحْتَهَآ﴾ (the one beneath her called her): it is the angel in both aspects alike, i.e. Gabriel called her from beneath her; and "the one beneath her called her": the one who was beneath her. His saying (سَرِيّاً): السرِىّ is a stream.

farraa:59-59.t: His saying: ﴿فَخَلَفَ مِن بَعْدِهِمْ﴾ khalf: khalf (with sukūn) is taken in the sense of blame, while khalaf (with fatḥa) is the righteous successor. Yet khalaf may occur for the bad and khalf for the righteous, because they sometimes take khalf to mean one generation after another.

farraa:25-25.t:
His saying: ﴿وَهُزِّىۤ إِلَيْكِ بِجِذْعِ ٱلنَّخْلَةِ﴾ (and shake toward you the trunk of the palm tree): the Arabs say هَزَّ بهِ and هزَّه (he shook it), خذ الخِطَام and خذ بالخِطَام (take the halter), تعلَّق زيدا and تعلَّق بزيد (cling to Zayd), خُذْ برأسه and خذ رأسه (take his head), and امدد بالحبل (and امدد الحبلَ) (stretch the rope). Allah said ﴿فَلْيَمْدُدْ بِسَبَبٍ إلى السَّمَاءِ﴾ (let him extend a rope to the ceiling); its meaning is: let him extend a rope (to the sky). Likewise in His saying ﴿وَهُزِّىۤ إِلَيْكِ بِجِذْعِ ٱلنَّخْلَةِ﴾, had it been وهُزّى جذعَ النخلة, it would have been correct.
His saying: ﴿يَسَّاقط﴾ (it will drop): it is also read ﴿تُسَاقِطْ عَلَيْكِ﴾, and تَسَاقط and تُسَاقِط (with tāʾ). Whoever read it يَسَّاقط referred it to the trunk. Al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib read it with yāʾ, and the companions of ʿAbdallāh (تساقط), meaning the palm; you may make it doubled if you wish, or light if you wish. And if you say ﴿تُسَاقِط عَلَيك﴾, it is correct. Doubled and light forms are both possible in the one beginning with tāʾ, while the doubled form alone is possible in the one beginning with yāʾ. Had a reader read تُسْقِط عليك رطبا (it will drop fresh dates on you), referring to the palm, or said يَسْقط عَليكِ رُطَباً, referring to the trunk, it would have been correct.
His saying (جَنِيّاً) (ripe): الجَنِىّ and المَجْنِىّ (picked) are one; it is (in sense) a passive participle (mafʿūl bihi).

farraa:61-61.t:
His saying: ﴿جَنَّاتِ عَدْنٍ﴾ is accusative (manṣūb). Had you put it in the nominative as a new beginning (istiʾnāf), it would have been correct.
His saying ﴿إِنَّهُ كَانَ وَعْدُهُ مَأْتِيّاً﴾: and He did not say ātiyan ("coming"). Everything that comes to you, you also come to it; do you not see that you say "I have come upon fifty years" and "fifty years have come upon me"? All of that is correct.

farraa:26-26.t: His saying: ﴿وَقَرِّي عَيْناً﴾ (and be content [lit. cool of eye]): it has come in the commentary: be of good cheer. "The eye" was made accusative only because the verb was originally its own, and you transferred it to the woman. Its meaning is: let your eye be cooled. When the verb is transferred from its owner to what precedes it, the owner of the verb is made accusative as an explanation (tafsīr, i.e. tamyīz (specification)). Similar is ﴿فَإنْ طِبْنَ لَكُمْ عَنْ شِىْءٍ مِنْهُ نَفساً﴾ (but if they willingly give up to you anything of it), whose meaning is only: if their souls are pleased «[Translator's note: the text has "طالت"; طابت is evidently meant.]» for you; and ضاق به ذَرْعاً and ضِقت به ذَرْعاً (he/I was distressed by it), and سؤت به ظَنّاً (I thought ill of him), which only (means: my opinion of him was bad). Likewise مررت برَجل حسنٍ وجهاً (I passed by a man handsome of face), whose meaning was only: his face was handsome; you transferred the verb of the face to the man, so "face" became the specifier. Build on this whatever you wish. His saying: ﴿إِنِّي نَذَرْتُ لِلرَّحْمَـٰنِ صَوْماً﴾ (indeed I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast): i.e. silence.

farraa:62-62.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَهُمْ رِزْقُهُمْ فِيهَا بُكْرَةً وَعَشِيّاً﴾: there is no morning and no evening there, but they are brought their provision according to the measures of morning and evening in this world.

farraa:27-27.t:
His saying: ﴿لَقَدْ جِئْتِ شَيْئاً فَرِيّاً﴾ (you have certainly done a thing unprecedented): الفرِىّ is a tremendous matter. The Arabs say: يَفْرِى الفَرِىّ (he does marvels) when someone does excellent work, or (excellent) watering, and surpasses people; this is said of him. The rajaz poet said:
قد أَطعمتنْى دَقَلاً حَجْرِيّاً * قد كنت تفرين به الفَرِيَّا
(You have fed me poor dates from Ḥajr — dates with which you used to do marvels.)
i.e. you used to eat them in great quantity.

farraa:64-64.t: His saying: ﴿وَمَا نَتَنَزَّلُ إِلاَّ بِأَمْرِ رَبِّكَ﴾ means the angels. And His saying: to Him belongs ﴿مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِينَا﴾ of the affair of this world, ﴿وَمَا خَلْفَنَا﴾ of the affair of the Hereafter, ﴿وَمَا بَيْنَ ذٰلِكَ﴾: it is said: what is between the two blasts (of the Trumpet), and between them are forty years.

farraa:28-28.t: His saying: ﴿يٰأُخْتَ هَارُونَ﴾ (O sister of Aaron): she had a brother called Aaron, one of the best of the Children of Israel, who was not from her parents; so it was said: O sister of Aaron in his righteousness. I.e. your brother is righteous and your parents are (well-known) parents — as a reproach to her; i.e. the people of your house are righteous, and you have committed a grave thing.

farraa:66-66.t: His saying: ﴿لَسَوْفَ أُخْرَجُ حَيّاً﴾ and (أُخْرُجُ) are two readings.

farraa:29-29.t: His saying: ﴿فَأَشَارَتْ إِلَيْهِ﴾ (so she pointed to him): to her son. It is said that the cradle (المهد) was her lap — حِجْرها and حَجْرها. It is also said: his bed. "Lap" is better.

farraa:67-67.t: His saying: ﴿أَوَلاَ يَذْكُرُ ٱلإِنْسَٰنُ﴾: in the reading of Ubayy it is (يَتَذَكَّرُ), while the readers — ʿĀṣim and others — have read (يَذْكُرُ).

farraa:31-32.t:
His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلَنِي مُبَارَكاً﴾ (and He has made me blessed): one from whom people learn wherever I am.
His saying: ﴿جَبَّاراً﴾ (a tyrant): الجبّار is one who kills in anger and strikes in anger.
His saying ﴿وَبَرّاً بِوَالِدَتِي﴾ (and dutiful to my mother): you make it accusative on the basis of "He made me a prophet, and made me dutiful", following on from "prophet"; as in His saying (وَجَزَاهُمْ بِمَا صَبَرُوا جَنَّةً وحَرِيراً) (and He will reward them for their patience with a garden and silk), then He said ﴿وَدَانِيَةً عَلَيهِمْ ظِلاَلُهَا﴾ (and near above them are its shades): (دانيةً) refers back to ﴿مُتَّكِئين فيهَا﴾ (reclining therein), just as البَرّ refers back to His saying ﴿نَبِيّاً﴾ (a prophet).

farraa:73-73.t: His saying: ﴿خَيْرٌ مَّقَاماً وَأَحْسَنُ نَدِيّاً﴾: an assembly (majlis). Al-nadiyy and al-nādī are two dialectal forms.

farraa:33-33.t: His saying: ﴿وَٱلسَّلاَمُ عَلَيَّ﴾ (and peace is on me): it has come in the commentary: safety is upon me.

farraa:74-74.t: His saying: ﴿أَحْسَنُ أَثَاثاً وَرِءْياً﴾: al-athāth is household goods (al-matāʿ), and al-riʾy is outward appearance. Al-athāth has no singular, just as al-matāʿ has no singular. The Arabs pluralize al-matāʿ as amtiʿa, amātīʿ and mutuʿ. Were you to pluralize al-athāth, you would say "three āththa", and uthath, nothing else. The people of Medina read it without hamza (وَرِيّاً), and that is a good option, because it comes with verses whose endings are not hamzated. It is also reported of some of them that they took al-riyy to be from rawītu ("I quenched my thirst"). Some read it (وَزِيّاً) with zāy; al-ziyy is form and appearance. The Arabs say: "qad zayyaytu the slave girl", i.e. I adorned her and dressed her up.

farraa:34-34.t:
His saying: ﴿قَوْلَ ٱلْحَقِّ﴾ (the word of truth): in the reading of ʿAbdallāh: (قالُ اللّهِ الحقُّ) (the word of Allah, the Truth); القول and القال have one meaning.
"The Truth" in this place means Allah. Had "the true word" been meant by it, with القول put in construct with الحقّ while meaning "the true word", it would have been correct, as it is said: ﴿إنَّ هَذَا لَهُوَ حَقُّ اليَقِين﴾ (indeed this is the truth of certainty), a thing being put in construct with its like. Similar is the saying of Allah ﴿وَعْدَ الصِّدْقِ الَّذِى كانُوا يُوعَدُونَ﴾ (the promise of truth which they had been promised), whose meaning is the true promise. Likewise ﴿ولَدَارُ الآخِرَةِ خَيْرٌ﴾ (and the home of the Hereafter is better), which is only: والدار الآخرةُ.
The readers have read with the accusative (قَوْلَ الحقّ), and it is common, meaning by it: truly (حَقّاً). And if you make القول accusative while intending it (to refer to) a description of Jesus, it would be correct, as though you said: هذا عبدالله أخاه بعينه (this is ʿAbdallāh, his very brother). The Arabs make the definite noun accusative in (sentences with) هذا, ذلك and their sisters; so they say: هذا عبدالله الأَسَدَ عادياً (this is ʿAbdallāh, the lion, attacking), just as they say: أسداً عاديا (a lion, attacking).

farraa:76-76.t: His saying: ﴿وَيَزِيدُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱهْتَدَواْ هُدًى﴾: through the abrogating and the abrogated.

farraa:35-35.t: His saying: ﴿مَا كَانَ للَّهِ أَن يَتَّخِذَ مِن وَلَدٍ﴾ (it is not [befitting] for Allah to take a son): (أن) is in the position of the nominative.

farraa:77-77.t:
His saying: ﴿أَفَرَأَيْتَ ٱلَّذِي﴾: without hamza.

His saying: ﴿لأُوتَيَنَّ مَالاً وَوَلَداً﴾: Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us: Muḥammad narrated to us: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us: al-Mughīra narrated to me from Ibrāhīm that he used to read (مَالُهُ وَوُلْدُهُ), and in Kāf-Hā-Yā-ʿAyn-Ṣād [Translator's note: i.e. Sūrat Maryam] (مَالاً ووُلْداً). Al-Farrāʾ said: Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb read likewise. ʿĀṣim gave the wāw a fatḥa, and read it with full vowels throughout the whole Qurʾān. Mujāhid read (مالُه ووُلْدُه إلاَّ خَسَاراً) [Translator's note: Sūrat Nūḥ 71:21] in the nominative, with fatḥa in the rest of the Qurʾān. The poet said:
ولقد رأيت معاشرا * قد ثَمّروا مَالاً ووُلْدَا
(I have seen groups of people who had made wealth and offspring grow.)
He used the light form [Translator's note: the parenthesis in the source reads «(وثَمروا)»; the light form meant is evidently وُلْد]. Al-wuld and al-walad are two dialectal forms, like (what they said): al-ʿadam and al-ʿudm (and al-wuld and al-walad), and they are one and the same (and not a plural). Among the proverbs of the Arabs: "وُلْدُكِ مَن دَمَّى عقبيكِ" (your child is the one who bloodied your heels). And one of the poets said:
فليت فلاناً مات فى بطن أمّه * وليت فلانا كان وُلْدَ حمار
(Would that so-and-so had died in his mother's belly, and would that so-and-so had been the offspring of a donkey.)
So this is a singular. Qays make al-wuld a plural and al-walad a singular.

farraa:36-36.t: His saying: ﴿وَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ﴾ (and indeed Allah): it is also read ﴿وأَنَّ اللهَ﴾. Whoever reads it with fatḥa means: that is (because) Allah is my Lord and your Lord. It may be nominative, and it may be (in interpretation) genitive, on the basis of "and because Allah", as He said ﴿ذَلِكَ أَنْ لَمْ يكُنْ رَبكَ مُهْلِكَ القُرَى بِظُلْمٍ﴾ (that is because your Lord would not destroy the towns for wrongdoing). Had you given (أنَّ) fatḥa on the basis of His saying ﴿وَأَوْصَانىِ بِالصَّلاَةِ والزكاةِ﴾ (and He has enjoined upon me prayer and zakāh) — (and that Allah…) — it would be a valid aspect. In the reading of Ubayy: (إِن الله ربّى وربّكم) without the wāw, and this is evidence that it has kasra.

farraa:80-80.t: His saying: ﴿وَنَرِثُهُ مَا يَقُولُ﴾ means: what al-ʿĀṣī ibn Wāʾil claims he will have in Paradise, so We give it to someone else. ﴿وَيَأْتِينَا فَرْداً﴾: devoid of wealth and children.

farraa:4-4.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَمْ أَكُنْ بِدُعَآئِكَ رَبِّ شَقِيّاً﴾ (and never have I been, in my supplication to You, my Lord, unhappy): he says: I have not been made wretched by calling on You; You answered me when I called You.

farraa:81-81.t: His saying: ﴿لِّيَكُونُواْ لَهُمْ عِزّاً﴾: He is saying: so that they might be intercessors for them in the Hereafter.

farraa:82-82.t: So Allah said: ﴿كَلاَّ سَيَكْفُرُونَ بِعِبَادَتِهِمْ وَيَكُونُونَ عَلَيْهِمْ ضِدّاً﴾: they will be helpers against them.

farraa:41-41.t: His saying: ﴿وَٱذْكُرْ فِي ٱلْكِتَابِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ﴾ (and mention in the Book Abraham): relate the story of Abraham; recite it to them. Likewise His saying regarding the prophets He mentioned, (i.e.) relate to them their stories.

farraa:83-83.t: His saying: ﴿أَنَّآ أَرْسَلْنَا ٱلشَّيَاطِينَ عَلَى ٱلْكَافِرِينَ﴾ (in this world) ﴿تَؤُزُّهُمْ أَزّاً﴾: they agitate them towards acts of disobedience and incite them to them.

farraa:45-45.t: His saying: ﴿إِنِّيۤ أَخَافُ أَن يَمَسَّكَ عَذَابٌ﴾ (indeed I fear that a punishment will touch you): He means: I know. It is like His saying ﴿فَخَشِينَا أَنْ يُرْهِقَهُمَا﴾ (and we feared that he would overburden them), i.e. and we knew.

farraa:84-84.t: His saying: ﴿إِنَّمَا نَعُدُّ لَهُمْ عَدّاً﴾: it is said: the days, the nights, the months and the years. Some of the exegetes said: the breaths.

farraa:46-46.t:
His saying: ﴿لأَرْجُمَنَّكَ﴾ (I will surely stone you): I will surely revile you.
His saying: ﴿وَٱهْجُرْنِي مَلِيّاً﴾ (and leave me for a long while): a long time. One says: I was with him مَلْوةً of time, and مُلْوةً, مِلْوةً and مُلاَوَةً of time. Hudhayl say مِلاوة, and some Arabs مَلاوة. All of it is from length.

farraa:85-85.t: His saying: ﴿نَحْشُرُ ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ إِلَى ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ وَفْداً﴾: al-wafd is riders (on mounts).

farraa:5-5.t: His saying: ﴿ٱلْمَوَالِيَ﴾ (the kinsmen): they are a man's (paternal cousins) and his heirs. الوَلِىّ and المَوْلى are one in the speech of the Arabs; in the reading of ʿAbdallāh: (إنَّمَا مَوْلاَكُمُ اللهُ ورَسُولَهُ) (your patron is only Allah and His Messenger) in place of (وَليُّكُمْ). It was mentioned regarding (the reading) خَفَّتِ الموالى (the kinsmen have become few) that it means "they became few"; it was reported from ʿUthmān (ibn ʿAffān).

farraa:86-86.t: His saying: ﴿وَنَسُوقُ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ إِلَىٰ جَهَنَّمَ وِرْداً﴾: on foot and thirsty.

farraa:6-6.t:
His saying: ﴿يَرِثُنِي﴾ (who will inherit from me): it is read in the jussive and in the nominative. Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb read it in the jussive, and the jussive is the (preferred) aspect, because (يرثنى) is in a verse other than the first, so the conditional answer (jazāʾ) is good. When you make it nominative, it is a ṣila (qualifying clause) of "the heir": "grant me one who will inherit from me". Similar are ﴿رِدْءًا يُصَدِّقُنِى﴾ (as a helper, confirming me) and ﴿يُصَدِّقْنِى﴾.
When you make an imperative fall upon an indefinite noun followed by a verb beginning with yāʾ, tāʾ, nūn or alif, there are two aspects in it: the jussive, as the answer of the condition; and the nominative, as a qualifying clause of the indefinite noun, in the role of الذى (who/which). As someone says: أعِرنى دابَّة أركبْها (lend me a mount and I will ride it) or, if you wish, أركبُها (a mount that I may ride). Likewise ﴿أَنْزِلْ علَيْنَا مَائِدَةً مِنَ السَّمَاءِ تَكُونُ لَنَا﴾ (send down to us a table from heaven to be for us); had He said (تَكُنْ لَنَا), it would have been correct. But when the verb after the indefinite noun does not pertain to the first (noun), and suppressing the hāʾ (pronoun) is not suitable in it — if the verb falls on the man — then only the jussive is possible; as you say: هَبْ لى ثوباً أَتَجَمَّل مع الناس (give me a garment, and I will look fine among people): (أتجمَّل) can only be jussive, because the hāʾ is not suitable in أتجمّل. And you say: أَعِرنى دابَّة أركبُ يا هذا (lend me a mount I may ride, you there), because you could say أركبُها, suppressing the hāʾ, so that is fitting.

farraa:87-87.t: His saying: ﴿لاَّ يَمْلِكُونَ ٱلشَّفَاعَةَ﴾: they will not have the power to intercede, ﴿إِلاَّ مَنِ ٱتَّخَذَ عِندَ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ عَهْداً﴾: and the covenant is "There is no god but Allah". (مَن) is in the position of the accusative (manṣūb) as the excepted (mustathnā); it cannot be genitive by an implied lām, but it is accusative carrying the sense of the genitive, just as you say in speech: "I wanted to pass by today, except the enemy, for I will not pass by him" — you except him according to the meaning; and had you made the bāʾ overt and said "I wanted to pass by, except by the enemy", you would have put it in the genitive. Likewise if it were said: "They will not have the power of intercession except for one who has taken with the Most Merciful [110 b] a covenant."

farraa:7-8.t:
His saying: ﴿لَمْ نَجْعَل لَّهُ مِن قَبْلُ سَمِيّاً﴾ (We have not assigned to any before this name): no one was named Yaḥyā before Yaḥyā son of Zechariah.
His saying: ﴿مِنَ ٱلْكِبَرِ عِتِيّاً﴾ (extreme old age) and (عِتيّا): Ibn ʿAbbās read (عُسِيّاً). You say of an old man when he has aged: قد عَتَا and عَسَا (he has become withered), as is said of a stick when it dries up.

farraa:89-89.t: His saying: ﴿ لَّقَدْ جِئْتُمْ شَيْئاً إِدّاً﴾: the readers read it with kasra on the alif, except Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, who read it with fatḥa (أَدّا). Some of the Arabs say: "You have brought something āddin (آدٍّ)", like māddin (مادّ). In all of its forms it means: something enormous.

farraa:9-9.t: His saying: ﴿قَالَ كَذٰلِكَ قَالَ رَبُّكَ هُوَ عَلَيَّ هَيِّنٌ﴾ (he said: "Thus [it will be]; your Lord says: It is easy for Me"): i.e. creating him is easy for Me.

farraa:90-90.t:
His saying: ﴿وَتَخِرُّ ٱلْجِبَالُ هَدّاً﴾: breaking apart.
His saying: ﴿يَتَفَطَّرْنَ مِنْهُ﴾, and yanfaṭirna. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [Translator's note: Ibn Masʿūd] it is (إن تكاد السَّموات لتتصَدَّع منه), and Ḥamza read it (يَنْفَطِرْنَ) in this sense.

farraa:91-91.t: His saying: ﴿أَن دَعَوْا﴾: because they ascribed, and for having ascribed. The position of (أَن) is accusative because of its being joined [Translator's note: i.e. joined directly to what precedes once the preposition is dropped]. Al-Kisāʾī used to say: (the position of أن) is genitive.

farraa:93-93.t: His saying: ﴿إِلاَّ آتِي ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ عَبْداً﴾: had you said "ātin al-Raḥmāna ʿabdan" (آتٍ الرحمن, with tanwīn and the accusative), it would have been correct, but I have not heard it from any reader.

farraa:96-96.t: His saying: ﴿وُدّاً﴾: Allah places love for them in the hearts of the believers.

farraa:98-98.t: His saying: ﴿أَوْ تَسْمَعُ لَهُمْ رِكْزاً﴾: al-rikz is a sound.

muyesser-irab:76-76.t:
﴿ويزيد الله الذين اهتدوا هدى﴾: the wāw is resumptive and the clause after it is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position; or the wāw is a conjunction, conjoining the clause to the conditional clause reported by "say", i.e.: "And say: Allah increases"; (ويزيد الله الذين اهتدوا) is an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) and mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause (اهتدوا) is the ṣila (relative clause) of (الذين), with no grammatical position; and (هدى) is a tamyīz (specification) or a second mafʿūl bihi of (يزيد).
﴿والباقيات الصالحات خير عند ربك ثوابا وخير مردا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; (الباقيات) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); (الصالحات) is a naʿt (adjective); (خير) is the khabar (predicate) of (الباقيات); (عند ربك): the adverb is attached to (خير); (ثوابًا) is a tamyīz; and (وخير مردًّا) is conjoined to (خير ثوابًا).

muyesser-irab:77-77.t: ﴿أفرأيت الذي كفر بآياتنا وقال لأوتين مالا وولدا﴾: the hamza is for interrogation, and the fāʾ is for immediate sequence (taʿqīb); (رأيت) here means "tell me", and (الذي) is its first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause (كفر بآياتنا) is the ṣila (relative clause) of (الذي), with no grammatical position; (وقال) is conjoined to (كفر); (لأوتين): the lām is the answer to an implied oath, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a hidden pronoun, its implied form being "I" (أنا); (مالًا) is the second mafʿūl bihi of (أوتين), and (ولدًا) is conjoined to ﴿مالًا﴾.

muyesser-irab:78-78.t: ﴿أطلع الغيب أم اتخذ عند الرحمن عهدا﴾: the hamza is for interrogation; (اطلع) is a past verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is "he", referring back to the disbeliever; (أم) is a conjunction counterbalancing the hamza; (اتخذ) is a past verb, and its fāʿil is latent (mustatir), referring back to him; (عند الرحمن) is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of (اتخذ), and (عهدًا) is the first mafʿūl bihi.

muyesser-irab:79-79.t: ﴿كلا سنكتب ما يقول ونمد له من العذاب مدا﴾: (كلا) is a particle of deterrence and rebuke; (سنكتب) is an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "we" (نحن); (ما) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause (يقول) is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position; (ونمد) is conjoined to (نكتب); ﴿له﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿نمد﴾; (من العذاب) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was an adjective of ﴿مدًّا﴾; and ﴿مدًّا﴾ is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), or a mafʿūl bihi if it has the meaning of "supply" (المدد).

muyesser-irab:80-80.t: ﴿ونرثه ما يقول ويأتينا فردا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; (ونرثه) is conjoined to (نمد), and the fāʿil (agent) is "we" (نحن); the hāʾ is accusative by removal of the preposition, and (ما) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the implied sense being: "and We shall inherit from him what he says"; or the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi and (ما) is a badal (substitute) of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) from the hāʾ, the meaning being: We shall inherit what he has of wealth, family and children; the clause (يقول) is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position; (ويأتينا) is conjoined to what precedes, and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he" (هو); (نا) is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl), fāʿil [Translator's note: so in the source; (نا) in (يأتينا) is in fact an attached pronoun in the position of the mafʿūl bihi, the fāʿil having just been given as the latent "he"]; and (فردًا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

muyesser-irab:81-81.t: ﴿واتخذوا من دون الله آلهة ليكونوا لهم عزا﴾: the wāw is resumptive; (اتخذوا) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object) is omitted, namely the idols understood from the context of the discourse; ﴿من دون الله﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); (آلهة) is the second mafʿūl bihi; (ليكونوا): the lām is the lām of causation (taʿlīl), and (يكونوا) is a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muḍmara) an after the lām; the interpreted maṣdar formed from an and the verb is genitive (majrūr) by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿اتخذوا﴾; the wāw is its noun (ism); ﴿لهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; and (عزًّا) is the khabar (predicate) of (يكونوا).

muyesser-irab:82-82.t: ﴿كلا سيكفرون بعبادتهم ويكونون عليهم ضدا﴾: (كلا) is a particle of deterrence and rebuke; (سيكفرون) is an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ); (بعبادتهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يكفرون﴾, an instance of the maṣdar (verbal noun) being annexed to its object; (ويكونون) is conjoined to (يكفرون), and the wāw is its noun (ism); ﴿عليهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); and (ضدًّا) is the khabar (predicate) of (يكونون).

muyesser-irab:83-83.t: ﴿ألم تر أنا أرسلنا الشياطين على الكافرين تؤزهم أزا﴾: (ألم): the hamza is for interrogation, and (لم) is a particle of negation, inversion [of tense] and jussive; (تر) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by (لم), and its fāʿil (agent) is "you" (أنت); (أن) together with what falls within its scope stands in place of the two objects of (تر); (أن) is an abrogating (nāsikh) particle, and ﴿نا﴾ is a pronoun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the accusative as the noun of inna; the clause (أرسلنا) is the khabar (predicate) of inna; (الشياطين) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause (تؤزهم) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause; and ﴿أزًّا﴾ is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative (manṣūb).

muyesser-irab:84-84.t: ﴿فلا تعجل عليهم إنما نعد لهم عدا﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an omitted condition); ﴿عليهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تعجل﴾; (إنما) is the restraining (kāffa) and restrained (makfūfa) particle; the clause (نعد لهم) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause; and (عدًّا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative (manṣūb).

muyesser-irab:85-85.t: ﴿يوم نحشر المتقين إلى الرحمن وفدا﴾: the adverb is made accusative by an omitted verb, its implied form being "remember" (اذكر); it is also said: (يوم) is made accusative by an implied [verb], i.e.: "on the day We gather and drive, We will do with the two groups what no description can encompass"; and it is also said: what governs it is His statement afterwards: ﴿لا يملكون﴾; the clause (نحشر) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the fāʿil (agent) of (نحشر) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "we" (نحن); (المتقين) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿إلى الرحمن﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) (نحشر); and (وفدًا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

muyesser-irab:86-86.t: ﴿ونسوق المجرمين إلى جهنم وردا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿نسوق المجرمين﴾ is a verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿إلى جهنم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿نسوق﴾; and ﴿وردا﴾ is a ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb) with the fatḥa.

muyesser-irab:87-87.t: ﴿لا يملكون الشفاعة إلا من اتخذ عند الرحمن عهدا﴾: the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; (لا) is negating; (يملكون) is an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), referring back to all people; (الشفاعة) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (إلا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); ﴿مَن﴾ is a relative noun whose position is nominative as a badal (substitute) from the wāw, or accusative as the excepted in a connected exception (istithnāʾ muttaṣil); the clause (اتخذ) is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿من﴾, with no grammatical position; (عند الرحمن) is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted [word] which is the second mafʿūl bihi of (اتخذ), and (عهدًا) is the first mafʿūl bihi; and it is also said: the exception is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ).

muyesser-irab:88-88.t: ﴿وقالوا اتخذ الرحمن ولدا﴾: the clause ﴿اتخذ الرحمن ولدًا﴾ is the content of the speech (maqūl al-qawl), and (اتخذ الرحمن ولدًا) is a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

muyesser-irab:89-89.t: ﴿لقد جئتم شيئا إدا﴾: the lām is the lām of the oath, and (قد) is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq); (جئتم) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); (شيئًا) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and (إدًّا) is a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:90-90.t: ﴿تكاد السماوات يتفطرن منه وتنشق الأرض وتخر الجبال هدا﴾: (تكاد) is one of the verbs of approximation (afʿāl al-muqāraba) that operate like kāna; (السماوات) is its noun (ism), and the clause (يتفطرن) is its khabar (predicate); the nūn is the fāʿil (agent); (منه) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يتفطرن﴾; (تنشق الأرض) is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; (تخر الجبال) is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; and (هدًّا) is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e.: "demolished"; or it stands in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because it has the meaning of the maṣdar; or it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e.: "because they are demolished".

muyesser-irab:91-91.t: ﴿أن دعوا للرحمن ولدا﴾: (أن) together with what falls within its scope is a maṣdar (verbal noun) that is a badal (substitute) from the hāʾ in (منه); or it is accusative by removal of the preposition, the preposition and its genitive noun being in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), since the demolition is explained as caused by their attributing a son to the All-Merciful; or it is the fāʿil (agent) of ﴿هدًّا﴾; (دعوا) is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif that was elided because of the meeting of two vowelless letters; (للرحمن) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) (دعوا); and (ولدًا) is the second object of (دعوا), the first being omitted, its implied form being "their object of worship" (معبودهم).

muyesser-irab:92-92.t: ﴿وما ينبغي للرحمن أن يتخذ ولدا﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) or a conjunction; ﴿ما﴾ is negating; ﴿ينبغي﴾ is an imperfect verb; ﴿للرحمن﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to it; ﴿أن﴾ is maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya); ﴿يتخذ﴾ is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb); the interpreted maṣdar from ﴿أن يتخذ﴾ is the fāʿil (agent) of ﴿ينبغي﴾; and (ولدًا) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

muyesser-irab:93-93.t: ﴿إن كل من في السماوات والأرض إلا آتي الرحمن عبدا﴾: (إن) is negating; (كل) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); (من) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿في السماوات والأرض﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted [word] that is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿من﴾, and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position; it is also said: (من) is an indefinite described by the preposition and its genitive noun, because it occurs after (كل), an indefinite; (إلا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (آتي الرحمن) is the khabar (predicate); and (عبدًا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent (mustatir) pronoun in (آتي).

muyesser-irab:94-94.t: ﴿لقد أحصاهم وعدهم عدا﴾: the lām occurs in the answer to an implied oath. ﴿قد﴾ is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq), and ﴿أحصاهم﴾ is a verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿عدهم﴾ is conjoined to (أحصاهم). ﴿عدًّا﴾ is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).

muyesser-irab:95-95.t: ﴿وكلهم آتيه يوم القيامة فردا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; (كلهم) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (آتيه) is the khabar (predicate); (يوم القيامة) is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) (آتيه); and (فردًا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

muyesser-irab:96-96.t: ﴿إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات سيجعل لهم الرحمن ودا﴾: (إن) is an abrogating (nāsikh) particle; (الذين) is a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the accusative as the noun of inna; the clause (آمنوا) is the ṣila (relative clause) of (الذين), with no grammatical position; the clause (عملوا الصالحات) is conjoined to (آمنوا); the clause (سيجعل) is the khabar (predicate) of inna; ﴿لهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted [word] that is the second object of (يجعل); (الرحمن) is the fāʿil (agent); and (ودًّا) is the first object of (يجعل).

muyesser-irab:97-97.t: ﴿فإنما يسرناه بلسانك لتبشر به المتقين وتنذر به قوما لدا﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an omitted condition); (إنما) is the restraining (kāffa) and restrained (makfūfa) particle; (يسرناه) is a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (بلسانك) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e.: "flowing"; (لتبشر): the lām is for causation (taʿlīl), and (تبشر) is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muḍmara) an after the lām of causation; the interpreted maṣdar from an and the verb is genitive (majrūr) by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿يسرناه﴾; ﴿به﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿تبشر﴾; (المتقين) is a mafʿūl bihi; (وتنذر) is conjoined (maʿṭūf); ﴿به﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿تنذر﴾; (قومًا) is a mafʿūl bihi; and (لدًّا) is a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:98-98.t:
﴿وكم أهلكنا قبلهم من قرن﴾: (كم) is the predicative (khabariyya) kam, an object placed before (أهلكنا); (قبلهم) is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أهلكنا﴾; and (من قرن) is a tamyīz (specification).
﴿هل تحس منهم من أحد أو تسمع لهم ركزا﴾: (هل) is a particle of interrogation; (تحس) is an imperfect verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you" (أنت); (منهم) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was an adjective of (أحد); (من) is a connective (ṣila) particle, and (أحد) is genitive by (من) in form and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) accusative in position; (أو) is a conjunction; (تسمع) is conjoined to (تحس); ﴿لهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl; and (ركزًا) is a mafʿūl bihi.

muyesser-irab:1-1.t: ﴿كهيعص‌﴾: the discussion of the disjointed letters (al-ḥurūf al-muqaṭṭaʿa) has preceded at the beginning of Sūrat al-Baqara.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t: ﴿ذكر رحمة ربك عبده زكريا﴾: (ذكر) is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject); (رحمة ربك) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), a case of the maṣdar (verbal noun) being put in construct with its object; (عبده) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of (رحمة); and (زكريا) is a badal (substitute) of (عبده), or a ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) of it.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t: ﴿إذ نادى ربه نداء خفيا﴾: ﴿إذ﴾ is an adverb of past time, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿رحمة﴾; the clause ﴿نادى﴾ is in the position of genitive by the adverb being put in construct with it; ﴿نادى﴾ is a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), implied as "he"; ﴿ربه﴾ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿نداء﴾ is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); and ﴿خفيًّا﴾ is an adjective.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿قال رب إني وهن العظم مني واشتعل الرأس شيبا﴾: (رب) is the one addressed (munādā), put in construct with the omitted yāʾ of the speaker; (إن) is an abrogating (nāsikh) particle; the yāʾ is an indeclinable (mabnī) pronoun in the position of accusative as the noun of (إن); the clause ﴿وهن العظم﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of (إن); ﴿مني﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); (اشتعل) is conjoined to (وهن); (الرأس) is the fāʿil (agent); and (شيبًا) is a tamyīz (specification) converted from the agent.
﴿ولم أكن بدعائك رب شقيا﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; (لم) is a particle of negation, conversion [to past] and jussive; (أكن) is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by (لم), its noun latent (mustatir), implied as "I"; (شقيًّا) is the khabar of (أكن), accusative (manṣūb); (بدعائك) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿شقيًّا﴾; and (رب) is the one addressed, put in construct with the omitted yāʾ of the speaker.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿وإني خفت الموالي من ورائي وكانت امرأتي عاقرا﴾: ﴿وإني﴾ is conjoined to ﴿إني وهن﴾; the yāʾ is the noun of (إن), and the clause ﴿خفت﴾ is its khabar (predicate); (الموالي) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿من ورائي﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿الموالي﴾, or to something omitted which is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of (الموالي), and the yāʾ is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وكانت امرأتي عاقرًا﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; (كان) is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb and the tāʾ is for the feminine; (امرأة) is the noun of (كان), nominative (marfūʿ), and the yāʾ is an indeclinable (mabnī) pronoun in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; and (عاقرا) is the khabar of (كان), accusative (manṣūb).
﴿فهب لي من لدنك وليا﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an omitted condition); (هب) is a verb of supplication; (لي) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿هب﴾; ﴿من لدنك﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; and (وليًّا) is the mafʿūl bihi of ﴿هب﴾.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t: ﴿يرثني ويرث من آل يعقوب واجعله رب رضيا﴾: the clause (يرثني) is an adjective of ﴿وليًّا﴾; (يرث) is conjoined to (يرثني); in ﴿من آل يعقوب﴾ the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يرث﴾, and the object is omitted, what is meant being inheritance of prophethood and knowledge; the yāʾ in ﴿يرثني﴾ is accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ); (اجعله) is a verb of supplication with a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent); (رب) is the one addressed (munādā), put in construct with the omitted yāʾ of the speaker; and (رضيًّا) is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of (اجعله).

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿يا زكريا إنا نبشرك بغلام اسمه يحيى﴾: (يا) is a vocative particle; (زكريا) is the one addressed (munādā), a proper name, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma; (إنا): (إن) is an abrogating (nāsikh) particle, and ﴿نا﴾ is an indeclinable pronoun in the position of accusative as the noun of (إن); the clause (نبشرك) is the khabar (predicate) of (إن), and the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (بغلام) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿نبشرك﴾; ﴿اسمه﴾ is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and ﴿يحيى﴾ its khabar, and the nominal clause is an adjective of (غلام).
﴿لم نجعل له من قبل سميا﴾: the clause is a second adjective of (غلام); ﴿له﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the omitted second object of (نجعل); ﴿من قبل﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); and (سميًّا) is the first object of (نجعل).

muyesser-irab:8-8.t: ﴿قال رب أنى يكون لي غلام وكانت امرأتي عاقرا وقد بلغت من الكبر عتيا﴾: (رب) is the one addressed (munādā), put in construct with the omitted yāʾ of the speaker; (أنى) is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as an adverb of place, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the [sense of] settledness in the khabar (predicate) of (يكون); (لي) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the omitted fronted khabar of (يكون), and (غلام) is its delayed noun. ﴿وكانت امرأتي عاقرًا﴾: the wāw is circumstantial; (كان) is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb and the tāʾ is for the feminine; (امرأة) is the noun of (كان), nominative (marfūʿ), and the yāʾ is an indeclinable (mabnī) pronoun in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (عاقرا) is the khabar of (كان), accusative (manṣūb); and the clause is circumstantial. (وقد بلغت من الكبر) is also a circumstantial clause; (من الكبر) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (بلغت), or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of ﴿عتيًّا﴾, because it was an adjective of it and was placed before it; and (عتيًّا) is the object of (بلغت).

muyesser-irab:9-9.t: ﴿قال كذلك قال ربك هو علي هين وقد خلقتك من قبل ولم تك شيئا﴾: ﴿قال﴾ is a past verb with a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent); in ﴿كذلك﴾ the kāf is a noun meaning "like", indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "the matter is thus", or in the position of accusative by ﴿قال﴾; in ﴿ذلك﴾, ﴿ذا﴾ is a demonstrative in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), the lām is for distance and the kāf is a particle of address, the reference being to something vague which is indicated by ﴿هو علي هين﴾; ﴿قال ربك﴾ is a verb and its fāʿil; ﴿هو﴾ is a mubtadaʾ; ﴿علي﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿هين﴾; ﴿هين﴾ is the khabar of ﴿هو﴾; (وقد): the wāw is circumstantial and (قد) is a particle of affirmation; (خلقتك) is a verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿من قبل﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿خلقتك﴾; the wāw is circumstantial; (لم) is a particle of negation, conversion [to past] and jussive; ﴿تك﴾ is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لم﴾, the sign of its jussive being the sukūn implied (muqaddar) on the nūn that was dropped for lightness; the noun of ﴿تك﴾ is latent; (شيئًا) is the khabar of (تك); and the clause (ولم تك شيئًا) is a nested ḥāl (circumstantial).

muyesser-irab:10-10.t:
﴿قال رب اجعل لي آية﴾: (رب) is the one addressed (munādā), put in construct with the omitted yāʾ of the speaker; (اجعل) is a verb of supplication; (لي) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and (آية) is the first mafʿūl bihi.
﴿قال آيتك ألا تكلم الناس ثلاث ليال سويا﴾: (آيتك) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); (أن) with what falls within its scope is the khabar (predicate); (الناس) is a mafʿūl bihi; ﴿ثلاث ليال﴾ is accusative as an adverb, the adverb being attached to ﴿تكلم﴾; and (سويًّا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent of (تكلم). It is also said: (سويًّا) is accusative as an adjective of ﴿ثلاث﴾, meaning that they are complete.

muyesser-irab:11-11.t: ﴿فخرج على قومه من المحراب فأوحى إليهم أن سبحوا بكرة وعشيا﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive. (خرج): a verb with a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent). ﴿على قومه﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿من المحراب﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿خرج﴾. ﴿فأوحى﴾: conjoined to ﴿خرج﴾. (إليهم): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿أوحى﴾. ﴿أن﴾ is maṣdariyya, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from (أن) and the verb is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿سبحوا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of maṣdariyya ﴿أن﴾, with no grammatical position. Or ﴿أن﴾ is explicative, and the clause after it is explicative with no grammatical position. (سبحوا): an imperative verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (بكرة): an adverb of time attached to ﴿سبح﴾; and (عشيًّا) is conjoined to ﴿بكرة﴾.

muyesser-irab:12-12.t:
﴿يا يحيى خذ الكتاب بقوة﴾: ﴿يا﴾ is a vocative particle; ﴿يحيى﴾ is the one addressed (munādā), a singular proper name; ﴿خذ الكتاب﴾ is an imperative verb with a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and ﴿بقوة﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent of (خذ), the bāʾ being for accompaniment (mulābasa), i.e. "you being endowed with strength and earnestness".
﴿وآتيناه الحكم صبيا﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position; (آتيناه) is a verb, its fāʿil and its first mafʿūl bihi; (الحكم) is the second mafʿūl bihi; and (صبيًّا) is a ḥāl of the hāʾ.

muyesser-irab:13-13.t: ﴿وحنانا من لدنا وزكاة وكان تقيا﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; (حنانًا) is conjoined to (الحكم), i.e. "and We gave him tenderness"; it is also said: it is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb; ﴿من لدنا﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted adjective of ﴿حنانًا﴾; (زكاة) is conjoined to ﴿حنانًا﴾; (كان تقيًا) is conjoined to (آتيناه); (كان) is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, its noun a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "he"; and (تقيًّا) is the khabar (predicate) of (كان), accusative (manṣūb).

muyesser-irab:14-14.t: ﴿وبرا بوالديه ولم يكن جبارا عصيا﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; (برًّا) is conjoined to ﴿تقيًّا﴾; (بوالديه) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿برًّا﴾; (لم يكن) is conjoined to (وكان تقيًّا); the noun of (يكن) is latent (mustatir), implied as "he"; (جبارًا) is its khabar (predicate); and (عصيًّا) is a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:15-15.t: ﴿وسلام عليه يوم ولد ويوم يموت ويوم يبعث حيا﴾: the wāw is resumptive; (سلام) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and beginning with it although it is indefinite is permissible because it contains [the sense of] supplication; (عليه) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate); (يوم) is an adverb attached to ﴿سلام﴾; the clause (ولد) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause ﴿وسلام عليه يوم ولد﴾ is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position, and what follows it is conjoined to it; and ﴿حيًّا﴾ is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

muyesser-irab:16-16.t: ﴿واذكر في الكتاب مريم إذ انتبذت﴾: the wāw is resumptive; (اذكر) is an imperative verb with a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent), implied as "you"; (في الكتاب) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (اذكر); (مريم) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿إذ﴾ is an adverb of past time attached to an omitted muḍāf, the implied form being "and mention the story of Maryam" or "the news of Maryam", so that the adverb is attached to that story or news. Or ﴿إذ﴾ is a noun indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of accusative as a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) of (مريم), the meaning being "mention the time of her withdrawing"; the clause ﴿انتبذت﴾ is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (من أهلها) is a ḥāl (circumstantial); (مكانًا) is an adverb attached to (انتبذت), i.e. "in a place", or a mafʿūl bihi on the view that (انتبذت) means "she came to"; (شرقيًّا) is a naʿt (adjective); and the clause ﴿واذكر في الكتاب مريم﴾ is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:17-17.t: ﴿فاتخذت من دونهم حجابا فأرسلنا إليها روحنا فتمثل لها بشرا سويا﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive; (اتخذت) is a past verb with a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent); (من دونهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (حجابًا) is the first mafʿūl bihi; ﴿فأرسلنا﴾ is conjoined to ﴿فاتخذت﴾; (إليها) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿أرسلنا﴾; (روحنا) is a mafʿūl bihi; (فتمثل) is also conjoined; ﴿لها﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿تمثل﴾; (بشرًا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial); (سويًّا) is a naʿt (adjective); and what made it permissible for the ḥāl to be a non-derived (jāmid) noun is its being qualified.

muyesser-irab:18-18.t: ﴿قالت إني أعوذ بالرحمن منك إن كنت تقيا﴾: (إن) is an abrogating (nāsikh) particle; the yāʾ is an indeclinable (mabnī) pronoun in the position of accusative as the noun of (إن); the clause (أعوذ) is the khabar (predicate) of (إن), and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); (بالرحمن) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أعوذ﴾; (منك) is a preposition and its genitive noun also attached to ﴿أعوذ﴾; (إن) is a jussive conditional particle; (كنت) is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, the tāʾ being an indeclinable pronoun in the position of nominative as the noun of (كان); (تقيًّا) is the khabar of (كان), accusative (manṣūb); and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted.

muyesser-irab:19-19.t: ﴿قال إنما أنا رسول ربك لأهب لك غلاما زكيا﴾: (إنما) is [inna] restraining and restrained (kāffa wa-makfūfa); (أنا) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); (رسول) is the khabar (predicate); ﴿ربك﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the lām is causal; (أهب) is an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muḍmara) an after the lām; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from (أن) and the verb is genitive by the lām, and the preposition with its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (رسول), or to an omitted verb, its implied form being "He sent me"; ﴿لك﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿أهب﴾; (غلامًا) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and (زكيًّا) is an adjective.

muyesser-irab:20-20.t: ﴿قالت أنى يكون لي غلام ولم يمسسني بشر ولم أك بغيا﴾: (أنى) is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as an adverb of place, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the [sense of] settledness in the khabar (predicate) of (يكون). ﴿ولم يمسسني﴾: the wāw is circumstantial; (لم) is a particle of negation, conversion [to past] and jussive; (يمسسني) is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by (لم); the yāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and (بشر) is the fāʿil (agent). ﴿ولم أك بغيًّا﴾: (لم) is a particle of negation, conversion [to past] and jussive; (أك) is an imperfect verb in the jussive, the sign of its jussive being the sukūn on the nūn that was dropped for lightness; the noun of (أك) is latent (mustatir); and (بغيًّا) is its khabar.

muyesser-irab:21-21.t:
﴿قال كذلك قال ربك هو علي هين﴾: (كذلك) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject); (قال ربك) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿هو﴾ is a mubtadaʾ; (علي) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿هين﴾; and (هين) is the khabar of (هو).
﴿ولنجعله آية للناس ورحمة منا وكان أمرا مقضيا﴾: (لنجعله) gives a cause, the thing caused being omitted, i.e. "We did that"; or it is conjoined to something implied, i.e. "so that We might show Our power by it, and so that We might make him a sign". (آية) is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿نجعله﴾; (للناس) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of (آية); and (رحمة منا) is conjoined to (آية). ﴿وكان أمرًا مقضيًّا﴾: (كان) is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, its noun a latent (mustatir) pronoun; (أمرا) is the khabar of (كان), accusative (manṣūb); and (مقضيًّا) is an adjective.

muyesser-irab:22-22.t: ﴿فحملته فانتبذت به مكانا قصيا﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive, joining to something omitted, the implied form being "so Jibrīl blew into the opening of her garment, and she conceived him"; (فانتبذت) is conjoined to (فحملته); ﴿به﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) something omitted in the place of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿مكانًا﴾ is an adverb of place attached to ﴿انتبذ﴾, or a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and (قصيًّا) is an adjective.

muyesser-irab:23-23.t:
﴿فأجاءها المخاض إلى جذع النخلة﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive; (أجاءها) is a past verb and a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (المخاض) is a delayed fāʿil (agent); ﴿إلى جذع﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); and (النخلة) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿قالت يا ليتني مت قبل هذا وكنت نسيا منسيا﴾: (يا) is a vocative particle with the one addressed omitted, or a particle of alerting; (ليت) is an abrogating (nāsikh) particle; the yāʾ is an indeclinable (mabnī) pronoun in the position of accusative as the noun of (ليت); the clause (مت) is the khabar (predicate) of (ليت), and it is a verb and its fāʿil; the adverb is accusative and attached to ﴿مت﴾, and (هذا) is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وكنت﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; (كان) is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, and the tāʾ is an indeclinable pronoun in the position of nominative as the noun of (كان); (نسيًا) is the khabar of (كان), accusative (manṣūb); and (منسيًّا) is a naʿt (adjective), or a tawkīd (emphasis) of ﴿نسيًا﴾, because it has its meaning.

muyesser-irab:24-24.t:
﴿فناداها من تحتها ألا تحزني﴾: the fāʾ: conjunctive. (ناداها): a verb, a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent) referring to the angel or to ʿĪsā. ﴿من تحتها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ناداها﴾, or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent. (أن) is explicative, and the clause after it is explicative with no grammatical position; (لا) is prohibitive, and (تحزني) is jussive (majzūm) by (لا). It is also said: ﴿أن﴾ is maṣdariyya and (تحزني) is accusative (manṣūb) by it, (لا) is negative, and (أن) with what follows it is accusative by removal of the preposition (bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), which is attached to the calling; and the clause ﴿لا تحزني﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of maṣdariyya ﴿أن﴾, with no grammatical position.
﴿قد جعل ربك تحتك سريا﴾: (قد) is a particle of affirmation; ﴿جعل ربك﴾ is a verb and its fāʿil; (تحتك) is an adverb attached to something omitted which is the second object of (جعل); and (سريًّا) is the first object.

muyesser-irab:25-25.t: ﴿وهزي إليك بجذع النخلة تساقط عليك رطبا جنيا﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; (هزي) is an imperative verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the weak letter [Translator's note: so in the source; the imperative هُزِّي is mabnī on the dropping of the nūn, as the source itself says of (قولي) in the next entry], and the yāʾ is the fāʿil (agent); (إليك) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿هزي﴾. ﴿بجذع النخلة﴾: the bāʾ is redundant (ṣila), and (جذع النخلة) is the object; (تساقط) is jussive (majzūm) in answer to the request; (عليك) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿تساقط﴾; (رطبًا) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and (جنيًّا) is an adjective.

muyesser-irab:26-26.t:
﴿فكلي واشربي وقري عينا﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an omitted condition); (كلي) is an imperative verb and the yāʾ is the fāʿil (agent); what follows is conjoined to it; and (عينًا) is a tamyīz (specification) converted from the agent, since the underlying form is "let your eye be cooled".
﴿فإما ترين من البشر أحدا﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive; (إن) is conditional, its nūn assimilated into ﴿ما﴾, and (ما) is redundant (ṣila); (ترين) is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), with the nūn of emphasis; ﴿من البشر﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was originally an adjective of ﴿أحدًا﴾; and (أحدًا) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿فقولي إني نذرت للرحمن صوما فلن أكلم اليوم إنسيا﴾: the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa) for the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (قولي) is an imperative verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the yāʾ is the fāʿil; (إن) is an abrogating (nāsikh) particle; the yāʾ is an indeclinable pronoun in the position of accusative as the noun of (إن); the clause (نذرت) is the khabar (predicate) of (إن), and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); (للرحمن) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿نذرت﴾; and (صومًا) is a mafʿūl bihi. ﴿فلن﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position; (لن) is a particle of negation, accusative and future; (أكلم) is accusative (manṣūb) by (لن); (اليوم) is an adverb attached to ﴿أكلم﴾; and (إنسيًّا) is a mafʿūl bihi.

muyesser-irab:27-27.t: ﴿فأتت به قومها تحمله قالوا يا مريم لقد جئت شيئا فريا﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive; (أتت) is a verb with a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent), and the tāʾ is for the feminine; ﴿به﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "accompanied by him", and it is said: attached to ﴿أتت﴾; (قومها) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause (تحمله) is a second ḥāl, either of the pronoun of Maryam or of the pronoun of ʿĪsā in (به); the clause ﴿فأتت...﴾ is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position; (قالوا) is a verb and its fāʿil; (يا) is a vocative particle and (مريم) is the one addressed (munādā); the lām is the answer to an omitted oath; (قد) is a particle of affirmation; (جئت) is a verb and its fāʿil; (شيئًا) is a mafʿūl bihi, i.e. "you have done a thing"; and (فريًّا) is a naʿt (adjective); it is also said: it is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a strange kind of coming".

muyesser-irab:28-28.t: ﴿يا أخت هارون ما كان أبوك امرأ سوء وما كانت أمك بغيا﴾: (يا) is a vocative particle, and ﴿أخت هارون﴾ is the one addressed (munādā), in construct (muḍāf). ﴿ما كان أبوك امرأ سوء﴾: (ما) is negative; (كان) is an abrogating (nāsikh) verb; (أبو) is the noun of (كان), nominative (marfūʿ) with the wāw because it is one of the five nouns; the kāf is an indeclinable (mabnī) pronoun in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (امرأ) is the khabar (predicate) of (كان), accusative (manṣūb); and (سوء) is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وما كانت أمك بغيًّا﴾ is conjoined to the clause preceding it.

muyesser-irab:29-29.t: ﴿فأشارت إليه قالوا كيف نكلم من كان في المهد صبيا﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive; (أشارت) is a verb with a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent); (إليه) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أشارت﴾; (قالوا) is a verb and its fāʿil; (كيف) is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); (نكلم) is an imperfect verb with a latent fāʿil; ﴿مَن﴾ is a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause (كان) is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿من﴾ with no grammatical position, and the noun of (كان) is latent; ﴿في المهد﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; and (صبيًّا) is the khabar (predicate) of (كان).

muyesser-irab:30-30.t: ﴿قال إني عبد الله آتاني الكتاب وجعلني نبيا﴾: the clause ﴿إني عبد الله﴾ is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); (إن) is an abrogating (nāsikh) particle; the yāʾ is an indeclinable (mabnī) pronoun in the position of accusative as the noun of (إن); (عبد الله) is the khabar (predicate) of (إن); the clause ﴿آتاني الكتاب﴾ is circumstantial, and (الكتاب) is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and ﴿جعلني نبيًّا﴾ is a past verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent) and its two objects.

muyesser-irab:31-31.t:
﴿وجعلني مباركا أين ما كنت﴾: ﴿وجعلني مباركًا﴾ is conjoined to ﴿وجعلني نبيًّا﴾; (أينما) is a jussive conditional noun in the position of accusative as an adverb of place, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (كان) is complete (tāmm) and the tāʾ is its fāʿil (agent); it is also said: it is incomplete (nāqiṣ), and (أينما) is attached to its omitted fronted khabar (predicate).
﴿وأوصاني بالصلاة والزكاة ما دمت حيا﴾: in ﴿ما دمت﴾, (ما) is maṣdariyya and temporal (ẓarfiyya); (دمت) is an incomplete past verb, the tāʾ is its noun, and (حيًّا) its khabar. The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from ﴿ما﴾ and the verb is accusative as an adverb, and the adverb is attached to ﴿أوصاني﴾.

muyesser-irab:32-32.t: ﴿وبرا بوالدتي ولم يجعلني جبارا شقيا﴾: [Translator's note: the source begins without naming the word parsed; it evidently refers to (برًّا).] a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being ﴿جعلني﴾; ﴿بوالدتي﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿برًّا﴾; ﴿ولم يجعلني﴾ is conjoined to ﴿وجعلني﴾; (جبارًا) is a second mafʿūl bihi; and (شقيًّا) is an adjective.

muyesser-irab:33-33.t: ﴿والسلام علي يوم ولدت ويوم أموت ويوم أبعث حيا﴾: (السلام) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿علي﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) its omitted khabar (predicate); (يوم) is an adverb attached to the sense of settledness to which the preposition and its genitive noun ﴿عليَّ﴾ are attached; the clause (ولدت) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (يوم أبعث) is conjoined to (يوم ولدت), and likewise (يوم أبعث) [Translator's note: so in the source; the first of these presumably should be (يوم أموت)]; and (حيًّا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

muyesser-irab:34-34.t: ﴿ذلك عيسى ابن مريم قول الحق الذي فيه يمترون﴾: (ذلك) is a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ (subject); (عيسى) is its khabar (predicate); ﴿ابن﴾ is a badal (substitute); ﴿مريم﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿قول﴾ is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, emphasising the content of the clause, i.e. "I say the word of truth"; ﴿الذي﴾ is a naʿt (adjective) of (القول) if ʿĪsā is meant by it, or an adjective of (الحق) itself; (فيه) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يمترون﴾; and the clause (فيه يمترون) is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:35-35.t:
﴿ما كان لله أن يتخذ من ولد سبحانه﴾: (ما) is negative; (كان) is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb; ﴿لله﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) its omitted fronted khabar (predicate); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from ﴿أن يتخذ﴾ is the noun of (كان); ﴿مِن﴾ is redundant (ṣila); (ولد) is genitive by (من) in form and accusative in position as mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and (سبحانه) stands in for a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative by an omitted verb, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿إذا قضى أمرا﴾: (إذا) is a future adverb; the clause (قضى) is in the position of genitive by being put in construct; and (أمرًا) is a mafʿūl bihi.
﴿فإنما يقول له كن فيكون﴾: the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa) for the answer of (إذا); the clause (إنما يقول) has no grammatical position because it is the answer of a non-jussive condition; ﴿له﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿يقول﴾; (كن) is a complete (tāmm) imperative verb, and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); the fāʾ is resumptive; (يكون) is a complete imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) with the ḍamma, its fāʿil (agent) being "it"; and the clause is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:36-36.t: ﴿وإن الله ربي وربكم فاعبدوه هذا صراط مستقيم﴾: the wāw is resumptive; (إن) is an abrogating (nāsikh) particle; the Divine Name is the noun of (إن), accusative (manṣūb); (ربي) is the khabar (predicate) of (إن); (ربكم) is conjoined to (ربي); (فاعبدوه): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an omitted condition); the clause ﴿وإن الله...﴾ is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position; (اعبدوه) is an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (هذا) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); (صراط) is the khabar; (مستقيم) is an adjective of (صراط); and the clause has no grammatical position because it is causal (taʿlīliyya).

muyesser-irab:37-37.t:
﴿فاختلف الأحزاب من بينهم﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position; (اختلف الأحزاب) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); and ﴿من بينهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of (الأحزاب).
﴿فويل للذين كفروا من مشهد يوم عظيم﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive; (ويل) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); (للذين) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the omitted khabar (predicate) of (ويل); the clause (كفروا) is the ṣila (relative clause) of (الذين), with no grammatical position; and (من مشهد) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿ويل﴾.

muyesser-irab:38-38.t: ﴿أسمع بهم وأبصر يوم يأتوننا لكن الظالمون اليوم في ضلال مبين﴾: (أسمع) is a past verb that has come in the form of the imperative, for exclamation (taʿajjub); the bāʾ is a redundant (ṣila) particle; the clause has no grammatical position because it is resumptive; ﴿يوم﴾ is an adverb of time, accusative (manṣūb) with the fatḥa, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أسمع وأبصر﴾; the clause ﴿يأتوننا﴾ is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (لكن) is lightened and inoperative (muhmala); (الظالمون) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); (اليوم) is an adverb of time, accusative with the fatḥa, attached to ﴿ضلال﴾; ﴿في ضلال﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar (predicate); and (مبين) is an adjective.

muyesser-irab:39-39.t: ﴿وأنذرهم يوم الحسرة إذ قضي الأمر وهم في غفلة وهم لا يؤمنون﴾: ﴿أنذرهم﴾ is an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), implied as "you"; the hāʾ is the object and the mīm the sign of the plural; ﴿يوم الحسرة﴾ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿إذ﴾ is a noun indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of accusative as a badal (substitute) of ﴿يوم﴾, or an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿الحسرة﴾. ﴿وهم﴾: the wāw is circumstantial; ﴿هم﴾ is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and ﴿في غفلة﴾ the khabar (predicate); ﴿وهم لا يؤمنون﴾ is also a circumstantial clause.

muyesser-irab:40-40.t: ﴿إنا نحن نرث الأرض ومن عليها وإلينا يرجعون﴾: (إن) is an abrogating (nāsikh) particle; ﴿نا﴾ is an indeclinable (mabnī) pronoun in the position of accusative as the noun of (إن); (نحن) is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the noun of (إن); the clause ﴿نرث الأرض﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of (إن); ﴿مَن﴾ is conjoined to (الأرض); ﴿عليها﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿مَن﴾, and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position. ﴿وإلينا﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿يرجعون﴾; the wāw is conjunctive; (يرجعون) is an imperfect verb whose agent is not named (passive), and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).

muyesser-irab:41-41.t:
﴿واذكر في الكتاب إبراهيم﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position; (اذكر) is an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), implied as "you"; (في الكتاب) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿اذكر﴾; and (إبراهيم) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿إنه كان صديقا نبيا﴾: (إن) is an abrogating (nāsikh) particle; the hāʾ is an indeclinable (mabnī) pronoun in the position of accusative as the noun of (إن); the clause (كان) is its khabar (predicate); the noun of (كان) is latent, implied as "he"; (صديقًا) is the first khabar of (كان), accusative (manṣūb), and (نبيًّا) the second khabar of (كان). The clause ﴿إنه كان صديقا نبيا﴾ is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of (إبراهيم); it is also said that it is parenthetical between the replaced word and the badal (substitute), for His words in the following ayah, ﴿إذ﴾, are a noun of time occurring as a badal of ﴿إبراهيم﴾; and it is said that it is resumptive. On its being parenthetical or resumptive, it has no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:42-42.t:
﴿إذ قال لأبيه يا أبت﴾: ﴿إذ﴾ is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿كان﴾ or to ﴿صديقًا نبيًّا﴾; or ﴿إذ﴾ is a noun indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of accusative as a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) of ﴿إبراهيم﴾; or ﴿إذ﴾ is an adverb attached to an omitted muḍāf, the implied form being "and mention the story of Ibrāhīm, or the news of Ibrāhīm, when he said to his father", so that the adverb is attached to that story or news. On taking ﴿إذ﴾ as a badal or as an adverb of an omitted muḍāf, the clause ﴿إنه كان صديقًا نبيًّا﴾ is parenthetical. The clause ﴿قال﴾ is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿لأبيه﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿قال﴾; ﴿يا﴾ is a vocative particle; and (أبت) is the one addressed (munādā), put in construct with the yāʾ of the speaker, for which the tāʾ has been substituted.
﴿لم تعبد ما لا يسمع ولا يبصر ولا يغني عنك شيئا﴾: ﴿لِمَ﴾ is originally the genitive lām and interrogative (ما), and it is attached together with its genitive noun to ﴿تعبد﴾; the fāʿil (agent) of (تعبد) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "you"; (ما) is a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause (لا يسمع) is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾ with no grammatical position, and what follows is conjoined to it; and (شيئًا) is a mafʿūl bihi, or stands in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).

muyesser-irab:43-43.t: ﴿يا أبت إني قد جاءني من العلم ما لم يأتك فاتبعني أهدك صراطا سويا﴾: ﴿يا أبت﴾: (يا) is a vocative particle, and (أبت) is the one addressed (munādā), put in construct with the yāʾ of the speaker, for which the tāʾ has been substituted; (إن) is an abrogating (nāsikh) particle; the yāʾ is an indeclinable (mabnī) pronoun in the position of accusative as the noun of (إن); the clause ﴿قد جاءني﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of (إن); ﴿من العلم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿جاءني﴾, (من) being partitive; (ما) is a relative noun, fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿لم يأتك﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾ with no grammatical position; in (فاتبعني) the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an omitted condition), and (اتبعني) is an imperative verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿أهدك﴾ is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) in answer to the request, and the kāf is a mafʿūl bihi; (صراطًا) is a second mafʿūl bihi, or accusative by removal of the preposition (bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ); and (سويًّا) is an adjective of ﴿صراطًا﴾.

muyesser-irab:44-44.t: ﴿يا أبت لا تعبد الشيطان إن الشيطان كان للرحمن عصيا﴾: ﴿يا أبت﴾: (يا) is a vocative particle, and (أبت) is the one addressed (munādā), put in construct with the yāʾ of the speaker, for which the tāʾ has been substituted; (لا) is prohibitive; (تعبد) is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive (لا), its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), implied as "you"; (الشيطان) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (إن) is an abrogating (nāsikh) particle; (الشيطان) is the noun of (إن), accusative (manṣūb); the clause (كان) is the khabar (predicate) of (إن), and the noun of (كان) is latent; (للرحمن) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿عصيًّا﴾; and (عصيًّا) is the khabar of (كان), accusative.

muyesser-irab:45-45.t: ﴿يا أبت إني أخاف أن يمسك عذاب من الرحمن فتكون للشيطان وليا﴾: (يا) is a vocative particle, and (أبت) is the one addressed (munādā), put in construct with the yāʾ of the speaker, for which the tāʾ has been substituted; (إن) is an abrogating (nāsikh) particle; the yāʾ is an indeclinable (mabnī) pronoun in the position of accusative as the noun of (إن); the clause (أخاف) is the khabar (predicate) of (إن); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from ﴿أن يمسك﴾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿أخاف﴾; (عذاب) is the fāʿil (agent) of (يمسك); ﴿من الرحمن﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted adjective of (عذاب); ﴿فتكون﴾ is conjoined to (أن يمسك); the noun of ﴿تكون﴾ is latent (mustatir), implied as "you"; ﴿للشيطان﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿وليًّا﴾; and ﴿وليًّا﴾ is the khabar of ﴿تكون﴾, accusative (manṣūb).

muyesser-irab:46-46.t:
﴿قال أراغب أنت عن آلهتي يا إبراهيم﴾: the hamza is interrogative; (راغب) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (أنت) is a fāʿil (agent) standing in place of the khabar (predicate); or (راغب) is a fronted khabar and (أنت) a delayed mubtadaʾ; (يا) is a vocative particle; and (إبراهيم) is the one addressed (munādā), a singular proper name, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma.
﴿لئن لم تنته لأرجمنك واهجرني مليا﴾: the lām paves the way for the oath (al-lām al-muwaṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam); (إن) is conditional; (لم) is a particle of negation, conversion [to past] and jussive; (تنته) is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by (لم); in (لأرجمنك) the lām occurs in the answer to the oath, and (أرجمنك) is an imperfect verb indeclinable on the fatḥa, its fāʿil latent (mustatir), implied as "I", and the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); in (واهجرني) the wāw is conjunctive, and (اهجرني) is conjoined to something omitted, the implied form being "so beware of me and leave me"; and ﴿مليًّا﴾ is an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿اهجرني﴾; it is also said: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent of (اهجرني).

muyesser-irab:47-47.t: ﴿قال سلام عليك سأستغفر لك ربي إنه كان بي حفيا﴾: (سلام) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and (عليك) the khabar (predicate). ﴿سأستغفر﴾: the sīn is for the future, and (أستغفر) is an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), implied as "I"; ﴿لك﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أستغفر﴾; (ربي) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause (إنه) is causal, with no grammatical position; (إن) is an abrogating (nāsikh) particle; the hāʾ is an indeclinable (mabnī) pronoun in the position of accusative as the noun of (إن); the clause (كان) is the khabar of (إن); the noun of (كان) is latent, implied as "he"; (حفيًّا) is the khabar of (إن) [Translator's note: so in the source; it is the khabar of (كان)]; and (بي) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿حفيًّا﴾.

muyesser-irab:48-48.t:
﴿وأعتزلكم وما تدعون من دون الله﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; (أعتزلكم) is a past verb [Translator's note: so in the source; (أعتزل) is an imperfect verb], the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (وما): the wāw is a conjunction, and (ما) is relative or maṣdariyya, and accusative by conjunction to the kāf, or a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment); the clause (تدعون) is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾ with no grammatical position; ﴿من دون الله﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); and the Divine Name is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿وأدعو ربي عسى ألا أكون بدعاء ربي شقيا﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; (أدعو) is conjoined to (أعتزلكم), its fāʿil latent, implied as "I"; (ربي) is a mafʿūl bihi; (عسى) is a past verb, one of the verbs of hope, its noun latent; (أن) with what falls within its scope is the khabar (predicate) of (عسى); (أكون) is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by (أن); the noun of (أكون) is latent, implied as "I"; (بدعاء) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿شقيًّا﴾; (ربي) is muḍāf ilayhi; and (شقيًّا) is the khabar of (أكون), accusative.

muyesser-irab:49-49.t: ﴿فلما اعتزلهم وما يعبدون من دون الله وهبنا له إسحاق ويعقوب وكلا جعلنا نبيا﴾: (لما) is an adverb of time meaning "when", or connective (rābiṭa); (اعتزلهم) is a past verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وما يعبدون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and (ما) is conjoined to the hāʾ, and it is relative or maṣdariyya; in ﴿من دون الله﴾ the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), and the Divine Name is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause ﴿وهبنا﴾ has no grammatical position because it is the answer of (لما); ﴿له﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿وهبنا﴾; (إسحق) is the object of (وهبنا); (يعقوب) is conjoined to (إسحق); (كلًّا) is the first mafʿūl bihi of ﴿جعلنا﴾; and (نبيًّا) is the second object.

muyesser-irab:50-50.t: ﴿ووهبنا لهم من رحمتنا وجعلنا لهم لسان صدق عليا﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; (وهبنا) is conjoined to the first (وهبنا); ﴿لهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿وهبنا﴾; (من رحمتنا) is a preposition and its genitive noun also attached to ﴿وهبنا﴾; (جعلنا) is conjoined to (وهبنا); ﴿لهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to something omitted in the place of the second object of (جعلنا); (لسان صدق) is the first object; and (عليًّا) is an adjective of (لسان).

muyesser-irab:51-51.t:
﴿واذكر في الكتاب موسى إنه كان مخلصا﴾: the wāw is resumptive; (اذكر) is an imperative verb with a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent), implied as "you"; (في الكتاب) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿اذكر﴾; (موسى) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿واذكر في الكتاب موسى﴾ is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position; (إن) is an abrogating (nāsikh) particle; the hāʾ is an accusative pronoun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative as the noun of (إن); and the clause ﴿كان...﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of (إن).
﴿وكان رسولا نبيا﴾: conjoined to the first (كان).

muyesser-irab:52-52.t: ﴿وناديناه من جانب الطور الأيمن وقربناه نجيا﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; (ناديناه) is conjoined to what preceded, and it is a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (من جانب) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿نادينا﴾; (الطور) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الأيمن) is an adjective of (جانب); (قربناه) is conjoined to (ناديناه); and ﴿نجيًّا﴾ is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of one of the two pronouns in (ناديناه) or (قربناه).

muyesser-irab:53-53.t: ﴿ووهبنا له من رحمتنا أخاه هارون نبيا﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; (وهبنا) is also conjoined; ﴿له﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿وهبنا﴾; (من رحمتنا) is a preposition and its genitive noun also attached to ﴿وهبنا﴾, (من) being partitive, i.e. "some of Our mercy", or causal, i.e. "because of Our mercy"; (أخاه) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿وهبنا﴾; (هارون) is a badal (substitute); and (نبيًّا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

muyesser-irab:54-54.t:
﴿واذكر في الكتاب إسماعيل﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position; (اذكر) is an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), implied as "you"; (في الكتاب) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿اذكر﴾; and (إسماعيل) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿إنه كان صادق الوعد﴾: (إن) is an abrogating (nāsikh) particle; the hāʾ is an indeclinable (mabnī) pronoun in the position of accusative as the noun of (إن); the clause ﴿كان صادق الوعد﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of (إن); the clause ﴿إنه كان...﴾ is causal; (كان) is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, its noun latent; (صادق) is the khabar of (كان), accusative (manṣūb); and (الوعد) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿وكان رسولا نبيا﴾: conjoined to the first (كان).

muyesser-irab:55-55.t: ﴿وكان يأمر أهله بالصلاة والزكاة وكان عند ربه مرضيا﴾: the clause (يأمر) is the khabar (predicate) of (كان); (أهله) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (بالصلاة) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يأمر﴾; (كان) is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, its noun latent (mustatir), implied as "he"; ﴿عند ربه﴾ is an adverb attached to ﴿مرضيًّا﴾; and (مرضيًّا) is the khabar of (كان), accusative (manṣūb).

muyesser-irab:56-56.t:
﴿واذكر في الكتاب إدريس﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position; (اذكر) is an imperative verb with a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent), implied as "you"; (في الكتاب) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿اذكر﴾; and (إدريس) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿إنه كان صديقا نبيا﴾: (إن) is an abrogating (nāsikh) particle; the hāʾ is an indeclinable (mabnī) pronoun in the position of accusative as the noun of (إن); and the clause (كان) is the khabar (predicate) of (إن).

muyesser-irab:57-57.t: ﴿ورفعناه مكانا عليا﴾: (رفعناه) is a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (مكانًا) is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿رفعناه﴾; and (عليًّا) is an adjective.

muyesser-irab:58-58.t:
﴿أولئك الذين أنعم الله عليهم من النبيين من ذرية آدم﴾: (أولئك) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); (الذين) is the khabar (predicate), or a badal (substitute) of the demonstrative; the clause ﴿أنعم الله عليهم﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of (الذين), with no grammatical position; ﴿من النبيين﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿من ذرية آدم﴾ is a badal with repetition of the preposition, the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to a ḥāl of the pronoun in (عليهم).
