﴿وممن حملنا مع نوح ومن ذرية إبراهيم وإسرائيل وممن هدينا واجتبينا﴾: conjoined to what preceded.
﴿إذا تتلى عليهم آيات الرحمن خروا سجدا وبكيا﴾: the clause ﴿إذا تتلى...﴾ together with its answer is resumptive, with no grammatical position, if you parse ﴿الذين﴾ as the khabar; but if you parse it as a badal, then the clause ﴿إذا تتلى﴾ is the khabar. The clause ﴿خروا﴾ has no grammatical position because it is the answer of (إذا); the wāw in (خروا) is the fāʿil (agent); (سجدًا) is a ḥāl of the agent; and (بكيًّا) is conjoined to ﴿سجدًا﴾.

muyesser-irab:59-59.t: ﴿فخلف من بعدهم خلف أضاعوا الصلاة واتبعوا الشهوات فسوف يلقون غيا﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive; (خلف) is a past verb; (من بعدهم) is a ḥāl (circumstantial); (خلف) is the fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿أضاعوا الصلاة﴾ is an adjective of (خلف); ﴿واتبعوا الشهوات﴾ is conjoined to ﴿أضاعوا الصلاة﴾; the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an omitted condition); (سوف) is a particle of the future; (يلقون) is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; and (غيًّا) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

muyesser-irab:60-60.t: ﴿إلا من تاب وآمن وعمل صالحا فأولئك يدخلون الجنة ولا يظلمون شيئا﴾: (إلا) is a particle of exception; ﴿من﴾ is the excepted (mustathnā), accusative (manṣūb); the clause (تاب) is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿من﴾ with no grammatical position; (آمن) is conjoined to (تاب), and (عمل) is also conjoined; (صالحًا) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿عمل﴾, or stands in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because it is an adjective of the maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "he did a righteous deed". In (فأولئك) the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an omitted condition); (أولئك) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause (يدخلون) is the khabar (predicate); (الجنة) is a mafʿūl bihi by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa); (لا يظلمون) is conjoined to (يدخلون); and (شيئًا) stands in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq, or is a second object, (يظلمون) being made to carry the sense of (ينقصون) "they are deprived".

muyesser-irab:61-61.t: ﴿جنات عدن التي وعد الرحمن عباده بالغيب﴾: (جنات) is a badal (substitute) of (الجنة); (عدن) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (التي) is an adjective of (جنات عدن); the clause (وعد) is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿التي﴾ with no grammatical position; (الرحمن) is the fāʿil (agent) of (وعد); (عباده) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and (بالغيب) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of (عباده), or a ḥāl of the pronoun of (الجنة), which is the pronoun returning to the relative noun, i.e. "He promised it to them while they are absent from it and do not see it".

muyesser-irab:62-62.t: ﴿لا يسمعون فيها لغوا إلا سلاما ولهم رزقهم فيها بكرة وعشيا﴾: the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of (جنات عدن); (لا) is negative; (يسمعون) is an imperfect verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (فيها) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "while they are in the Garden"; (لغوًا) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (إلا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (سلامًا) is a badal (substitute) of ﴿لغوًا﴾, or a disjoined (munqaṭiʿ) excepted; ﴿لهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); (رزقهم) is a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject); (فيها) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; (بكرة) is an adverb attached to the sense of settledness latent in the fronted khabar; and (عشيًّا) is conjoined to (بكرة).

muyesser-irab:63-63.t: ﴿تلك الجنة التي نورث من عبادنا من كان تقيا﴾: the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ (subject); (الجنة) is the khabar (predicate); (التي) is an adjective of (الجنة); the clause (نورث) is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿التي﴾ with no grammatical position; ﴿مَن﴾ is a relative noun, the object of (نورث); the clause (كان) is the ṣila of ﴿من﴾ with no grammatical position; the noun of (كان) is latent (mustatir), implied as "he"; and (تقيًّا) is the khabar of (كان).

muyesser-irab:64-64.t:
﴿وما نتنزل إلا بأمر ربك﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position; (ما) is negative; (نتنزل) is an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), implied as "we"; ﴿إلا بأمر ربك﴾ is an exception from the most general of states, so (إلا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr), and (بأمر) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿وما كان ربك نسيا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; (ما) is negative; (كان) is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb; (ربك) is the noun of (كان), nominative; and (نسيا) is the khabar (predicate) of (كان), accusative (manṣūb).

muyesser-irab:65-65.t:
﴿رب السماوات والأرض وما بينهما﴾: (رب السماوات والأرض) is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "He is the Lord of the heavens and the earth", or a badal (substitute) of (ربك).
﴿فاعبده واصطبر لعبادته هل تعلم له سميا﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an omitted condition); (اصطبر) is conjoined to ﴿اعبده﴾; (لعبادته) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿اصطبر﴾; (هل) is an interrogative particle meaning negation; (تعلم) is an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), implied as "you"; and (سميًّا) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

muyesser-irab:66-66.t: ﴿ويقول الإنسان أئذا ما مت لسوف أخرج حيا﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position; (يقول الإنسان) is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent), the al in it being generic; the hamza is interrogative with the meaning of negation; (إذا) is an adverb of future time, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb indicated by His words (لسوف أخرج), because the lām prevents attaching it to the mentioned ﴿أخرج﴾, since what comes after it does not govern what comes before it; (ما) is redundant (ṣila); the lām is the lām of inception (lām al-ibtidāʾ); (سوف) is a particle of the future; (أخرج) is an imperfect verb whose agent is not named (passive), and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir), implied as "I"; and (حيًّا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

muyesser-irab:67-67.t: ﴿أولا يذكر الإنسان أنا خلقناه من قبل ولم يك شيئا﴾: in ﴿أوَلا﴾ the hamza is interrogative, the wāw conjunctive and (لا) negative; (يذكر) is an imperfect verb conjoined to (يقول); (الإنسان) is the fāʿil (agent); (أنا): (أن) is an abrogating (nāsikh) particle, and ﴿نا﴾ is an indeclinable (mabnī) pronoun in the position of accusative as the noun of (أن); the clause (خلقناه) is the khabar (predicate) of (أن); (أن) and what follows it are interpretable as a maṣdar (verbal noun), the object of (يذكر); in (من قبل) the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يذكر﴾; (لم) is a particle of negation, conversion [to past] and jussive; (يك) is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by (لم), the sign of its jussive being the sukūn implied (muqaddar) on the nūn dropped for lightness; its noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "he"; (شيئًا) is the khabar of (يك), accusative (manṣūb); and the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) is omitted, its implied form being ﴿قبل الحالة التي هو فيها﴾ ("before the state he is in"), while some supplied ﴿قبل بعثه﴾ ("before his resurrection").

muyesser-irab:68-68.t:
﴿فوربك لنحشرنهم والشياطين﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive; the wāw is for the oath; (ربك) is genitive by the wāw of the oath, and the preposition with its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being "I swear"; the lām occurs in the answer to the oath; (نحشرنهم) is an imperfect verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis; the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "We"; the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and (الشياطين) is conjoined to the hāʾ, or the wāw means "with" and (الشياطين) is a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment).
﴿ثم لنحضرنهم حول جهنم جثيا﴾: (ثم) is a conjunction for delay; (لنحضرنهم) is conjoined to (لنحشرنهم); (حول) is an adverb of place attached to ﴿نحضرنهم﴾; (جهنم) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and (جثيًّا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

muyesser-irab:69-69.t: ﴿ثم لننزعن من كل شيعة أيهم أشد على الرحمن عتيا﴾: (ثم لننزعن) is conjoined to (لنحضرنهم); (من كل شيعة) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ننزعن﴾; (أيهم) is a relative noun meaning (الذي) "the one who", the first part of its ṣila (relative clause) having been omitted, and it is indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of (لنزعن) [Translator's note: so in the source, for (لننزعن)]; (أشد) is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause is the ṣila of ﴿أي﴾ with no grammatical position; (عتيًّا) is a tamyīz (specification); and (على الرحمن) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿أشد﴾, or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial).

muyesser-irab:70-70.t: ﴿ثم لنحن أعلم بالذين هم أولى بها صليا﴾: (ثم) is a conjunction for order and delay; the lām is for inception (lām al-ibtidāʾ); (نحن) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); (أعلم) is the khabar (predicate); (بالذين) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أعلم﴾; ﴿هم﴾ is a mubtadaʾ and (أولى) the khabar, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of (الذين), with no grammatical position; ﴿بها﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿أولى﴾; and (صليًّا) is a tamyīz (specification); it is also said: (صليًّا) is the plural of (صالٍ) and is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

muyesser-irab:71-71.t: ﴿وإن منكم إلا واردها كان على ربك حتما مقضيا﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; (إن) is negative; (منكم) is an adjective of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "anyone", i.e. "there is not anyone of you"; (إلا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (واردها) is the khabar (predicate); (كان) is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, its noun a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "it", i.e. the coming [to it]; (حتمًا) is the khabar of (كان), accusative (manṣūb); and (مقضيًّا) is an adjective of ﴿حتمًا﴾.

muyesser-irab:72-72.t: ﴿ثم ننجي الذين اتقوا ونذر الظالمين فيها جثيا﴾: (ثم ننجي) is conjoined to what preceded; the fāʿil (agent) of (ننجي) is latent (mustatir), implied as "We"; (الذين) is a relative noun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (اتقوا) is the ṣila (relative clause) of (الذين), with no grammatical position; (نذر) is conjoined to (ننجي), its fāʿil latent, implied as "We"; (الظالمين) is a mafʿūl bihi; (فيها) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (نذر) or to ﴿جثيًّا﴾; it is also said: attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of ﴿جثيًّا﴾, because it was originally an adjective of an indefinite noun and was placed before it, so it became accusative as a ḥāl; and (جثيًّا) is a ḥāl, or a second object of (نذر), i.e. "We leave them in it on their knees".

muyesser-irab:73-73.t:
﴿وإذا تتلى عليهم آياتنا بينات قال الذين كفروا﴾: the wāw is resumptive; (إذا) is a future adverb containing the sense of a condition; the clause (تتلى) is in the position of genitive by the adverb being put in construct with it; ﴿عليهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تتلى﴾; (آياتنا) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (بينات) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of (آياتنا); and the clause (قال الذين كفروا) has no grammatical position because it is an answer.
﴿للذين آمنوا أي الفريقين خير مقاما وأحسن نديا﴾: (للذين آمنوا) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (قال); the clause (آمنوا) is the ṣila (relative clause) of (الذين), with no grammatical position; (أي) is interrogative, mubtadaʾ (subject); (خير) is the khabar (predicate); (مقامًا) is a tamyīz (specification); (أحسن) is conjoined to (خير); (نديًّا) is a tamyīz; and the clause ﴿وإذا تتلى عليهم...﴾ is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:74-74.t: ﴿وكم أهلكنا قبلهم من قرن هم أحسن أثاثا ورئيا﴾: (كم) is the declarative [kam] (khabariyya), in the position of accusative as the object of (أهلكنا); (أهلكنا) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); (من قرن) is a non-explicit tamyīz (specification) of ﴿كم﴾; ﴿هم﴾ is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and (أحسن) the khabar (predicate), and the clause is in the position of accusative as an adjective of ﴿قرن﴾ [Translator's note: so in the source; (قرن) is genitive after (من)]; (أثاثًا) is a tamyīz; and (رئيًا) is conjoined to it.

muyesser-irab:75-75.t:
﴿قل من كان في الضلالة فليمدد له الرحمن مدا﴾: (من) is a jussive conditional noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); (كان) is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and it is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, its noun latent (mustatir), referring back to (من); (في الضلالة) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of (كان); the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa) for the answer; the lām is the lām of command; (يمدد) is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by the lām of command; ﴿له﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿يمدد﴾; (الرحمن) is the fāʿil (agent); and (مدًّا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative (manṣūb).
﴿حتى إذا رأوا ما يوعدون إما العذاب وإما الساعة﴾: (حتى) is a particle of limit and genitive, and the preposition with its genitive noun is attached to the answer, which is (فسيعلمون); it is also said: it is a particle of inception (ḥarf ibtidāʾ); the clause (رأوا) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (ما) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause (يوعدون) is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾ with no grammatical position; (إما) is a particle of condition and detailing; and (العذاب) and (الساعة) are a badal (substitute) of (ما).
﴿فسيعلمون من هو شر مكانا وأضعف جندا﴾: the fāʾ occurs in the answer of (إذا); (سيعلمون) is an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil; (من) is relative, mafʿūl bihi; ﴿هو﴾ is a mubtadaʾ and (شر) the khabar, and the clause is the ṣila of ﴿من﴾ with no grammatical position. It is also said: (من) is interrogative, in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ; ﴿هو﴾ is a second mubtadaʾ; (شر) is the khabar of the second mubtadaʾ; ﴿هو﴾ with its khabar is the khabar of ﴿من﴾; and the clause is attached to (رأوا) [Translator's note: so in the source; presumably what is meant is that the clause suspends (يعلمون), since it then says the clause is its object], and it is in the position of accusative as the object of (يعلمون).

nahhas-irab:1-1.t:
Abū Jaʿfar said: there is no disagreement about pronouncing it with sukūn (vowellessness). Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: it was given sukūn because these are letters of spelling, in which the pause is intended. The people of Medina read it between tafkhīm (full pronunciation) and imāla (inclination toward "e"). Muḥammad ibn Saʿdān related from Abū Muḥammad from Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ that he read كهيعص with the yā inclined (imāla), the hā between tafkhīm and imāla, and the ṣād assimilated. Abū ʿUbayd reported that Ḥamza used to incline the yā and pronounce the hā fully, and that ʿĀṣim and al-Kisāʾī used to give kasra-inclination to both the hā and the yā. Khārija reported that al-Ḥasan used to pronounce kāf with ḍamma; someone else reported that he used to pronounce «hā» with ḍamma; and Ismāʿīl ibn Isḥāq reported that al-Ḥasan used to pronounce yā with ḍamma. Abū Ḥātim said: ḍamma is not permissible on the kāf, nor on the hā, nor on the yā. Abū Jaʿfar said:
The reading of the people of Medina is among the best there is on this. Imāla is permissible in «hā» and «yā» and what resembles them, such as bā, tā and thā when shortened; this is the view of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh. He said: ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān told me that the Basrans are alone in discussing imāla, and that the Kufans did not mention it as they mentioned other parts of grammar. Imāla is permissible, according to Sībawayh and al-Khalīl, in what we have mentioned only because these are names of what is written, so they distinguished between them and particles such as «لا» and «ما»; whoever inclines any of these [particles] is in error, and likewise «ما» meaning «which» (الذي). He does not permit «حتّى» to be inclined, nor «إلّا» of exception, because both are particles; but if you name something with them, imāla becomes permissible. They (the two) permitted it in «أنّى» because it is an adverbial noun, like أين and كيف. Imāla of «kāf» is not permissible because the alif is in the middle. As for the reading of al-Ḥasan, it has puzzled a number of people, so that they said it is not permissible, among them Abū Ḥātim. The correct account of it is what Hārūn the reader explained.
He said: al-Ḥasan used to give a trace (ishmām) of the ḍamma — meaning that he would hint at it, just as Sībawayh reported that some Arabs say الصلاة and الزكاة hinting toward the wāw; and for this reason they are written in the muṣḥafs with wāw.

nahhas-irab:10-10.t:
قالَ آيَتُكَ: mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is (أن) with its ṣila. تُكَلِّمَ: accusative by أن, because «لا» does not intervene [as a barrier]. Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ permitted «أن لا تكلّمُ الناس» in the nominative, meaning «that you will not speak to people» (أنك لا تكلم الناس), as [the poet] said: [al-Ṭawīl] 282-
ألا زعمت بسباسة اليوم أنّني ... كبرت وأن لا يشهد اللهو أمثالي
(Basbāsa claimed today that I have grown old, and that men like me do not attend amusement.)
Al-Akhfash said: سَوِيًّا is accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial). Abū Jaʿfar said: the meaning is: he refrains from speech in this condition.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: فَأَوْحى إِلَيْهِمْ أَنْ سَبِّحُوا بُكْرَةً وَعَشِيًّا: two adverbials (ẓarf). Al-Farrāʾ claimed that العشيّ is feminine, and may be masculine when used vaguely. He said: العشيّ may also be the plural of عشيّة.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: يا يَحْيى خُذِ الْكِتابَ بِقُوَّةٍ: from أخذ يأخذ. The original is أؤخذ; the second hamza was dropped because of frequent use — and it was said, because two guttural letters come together — and the [initial] hamza was then dispensed with, and the dhāl was given kasra because of the meeting of two vowelless letters. وَآتَيْناهُ الْحُكْمَ صَبِيًّا: as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:13-13.t:
وَحَناناً: conjoined to الحكم. There are two views from Ibn ʿAbbās on its meaning. One, he said:
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, inclined toward him with mercy; the other view: the mercy toward people he was given, so that he might rescue them from disbelief and evil. وَزَكاةً: there are two views on its meaning. One is that he was given increase and growth in good; the other is that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, declared him pure by describing him as pure and God-fearing, for He, Mighty and Majestic, said: وَكانَ تَقِيًّا.

nahhas-irab:15-15.t:
وَسَلامٌ عَلَيْهِ
Nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); beginning with an indefinite noun is acceptable because it carries the meaning of a supplication.
The meaning of «سلام عليك» and «سلام الله عليك» is the same in the language.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t:
ذِكْرُ رَحْمَتِ رَبِّكَ: there are three views on its nominative case. Al-Farrāʾ said: it is nominative by كهيعص. Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: this is impossible, because «كهيعص» is not among what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, informed us about Zakariyyā; Allah, Mighty and Majestic, gave information about him and about the good news He gave him, and «كهيعص» is not part of his story. Al-Akhfash said:
the implied meaning is: «Among what We relate to you is the mention of the mercy of your Lord». The third view is that the meaning is: «This which We recite to you is the mention of the mercy of your Lord to His servant». رحمة is written with hāʾ, and one pauses on it [with hāʾ], and likewise everything like it. We know of no disagreement among the grammarians on this, outside poetry; indeed they have argued that this hāʾ is for the feminine of nouns, and distinguished between it and [the tāʾ of] verbs.
Al-Akhfash said: عَبْدَهُ is accusative by رحمة (the maṣdar). زَكَرِيَّا is a badal (substitute) for it, and it is a diptote because it contains the alif of the feminine. This is for whoever makes it a derived Arabic word, who does not inflect it as triptote either as definite or indefinite; whoever makes it a foreign word inflects it as triptote when indefinite.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: إِذْ: in the position of the accusative as an adverbial (ẓarf). نادى رَبَّهُ نِداءً: an emphatic maṣdar (verbal noun). خَفِيًّا: its naʿt (adjective).

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: قالَ رَبِّ إِنِّي وَهَنَ الْعَظْمُ مِنِّي: the imperfect is يهن, originally يوهن; the wāw was dropped because it falls between a yāʾ and a kasra. وَاشْتَعَلَ الرَّأْسُ شَيْباً: there are two views on its accusative. One is that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), because the meaning of اشتعل is «became white-haired» (شاب); this is the view of al-Akhfash Saʿīd. Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: it is accusative as tamyīz (specification). The view of al-Akhfash is preferable, because it is derived from a verb, and [treating it as] a maṣdar suits it better. وَلَمْ أَكُنْ بِدُعائِكَ رَبِّ شَقِيًّا: [شقيا is] the khabar (predicate) of أكن.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t:
وَإِنِّي خِفْتُ الْمَوالِيَ مِنْ وَرائِي: [الموالي is] accusative by خفت. The yāʾ was given a vowel in the accusative position because of its lightness, and given sukūn in the nominative and genitive positions because of their heaviness. It is related that ʿUthmān, may Allah be pleased with him, read خفّت الموالي من ورائي («the kinsmen have become few after me»); this is an irregular (shādhdh) reading, related only by Kaʿb, the client of Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ, from Saʿīd from ʿUthmān, and it is very far-fetched. Some scholars have claimed it is not permissible.
He said: how could he say «the kinsmen have become few after my death» while he is alive? The interpretation of it is that by «من ورائي» he does not mean «after my death» but «behind me» at that time. This too is far-fetched; it would need evidence that they had become few and scarce at that time, whereas Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has told about them what indicates their great number, when they said: «Which of them will take charge of Maryam?» وَكانَتِ امْرَأَتِي عاقِراً: that is, she does not give birth, as though she had a wound (ʿaqr).
The verb from it, عقرت, is heard from the Arabs, and the analogical form is عقرت. «[Translator's note: the two forms are written identically without vowels in the source; presumably ʿaqurat as heard and ʿaqarat as analogical, or vice versa.]» فَهَبْ لِي مِنْ لَدُنْكَ وَلِيًّا: the imperfect is يهب, originally يوهب with kasra on the hāʾ. Whoever says the original is يوهب with fatḥa on the hāʾ is mistaken, because if it were as he says, the wāw would not have been dropped, just as it is not dropped in يوجل. The wāw was dropped only because it falls between a yāʾ and a kasra; then [the hāʾ] was given fatḥa after its dropping because it contains one of the guttural letters.
The people of the two Sanctuaries (Mecca and Medina), al-Ḥasan, ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza read يَرِثُنِي وَيَرِثُ مِنْ آلِ يَعْقُوبَ with both in the nominative; Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar, Abū ʿAmr, Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash and al-Kisāʾī read يرثْني ويرثْ من آل يعقوب with both in the jussive. Abū Jaʿfar said: the first reading, with the nominative, is preferable and better in Arabic, and the argument for it is what Abū ʿUbayd said, for his argument is good. He said: the meaning is:
«Grant me from Yourself the heir (walī) whose condition and description is this», because among heirs (awliyāʾ) there are some who do not inherit; so he said:
«Grant the one who will be my heir». He rejected the jussive because its meaning is «if You grant him to me he will inherit from me» — so how could he inform Allah, Mighty and Majestic, of this when He knows it better than he does? This is a cogent argument, because the answer to an imperative, according to the grammarians, carries the meaning of condition and requital. You say: أطع الله جلّ وعزّ يدخلك الجنة («obey Allah, Mighty and Majestic, [and] He will admit you to Paradise»), meaning: «if you obey Him, He will admit you to Paradise». As for the meaning of يَرِثُنِي وَيَرِثُ مِنْ آلِ يَعْقُوبَ, the scholars have three answers on it:
It was said: it is inheritance of prophethood; it was said: it is inheritance of wisdom; and it was said: it is inheritance of wealth. As for their saying "inheritance of prophethood", it is impossible, because prophethood is not inherited; if it were inherited, someone would say: all people are descended from Nūḥ, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and he was a prophet sent [as messenger]. Inheritance of wisdom and knowledge is a good position; in the ḥadīth: «The scholars are the heirs of the prophets». As for inheritance of wealth, it is not excluded, even though some people have denied it on account of the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: «We are not inherited from; what we leave is charity». There is no proof in this, because a single person may speak of himself in the plural; and this may be interpreted as meaning «what we have left as charity is not inherited», because the Prophet ﷺ did not leave behind anything to be inherited from him; rather, what was his was something Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made permissible for him during his lifetime, by His saying, Majestic and Mighty: وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّما غَنِمْتُمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ فَأَنَّ لِلَّهِ خُمُسَهُ وَلِلرَّسُولِ [al-Anfāl: 41], since the meaning of «for Allah, Mighty and Majestic» is «for the ways of Allah, exalted be His praise», and among the ways of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is what serves the interest of the Messenger ﷺ as long as he lives. If it is said: in some narrations there is «We, the company of prophets, are not inherited from; what we leave is charity», then both interpretations apply to it: that «ما» means «which» (الذي), and the other, that one whose condition is this is not inherited from. مِنْ آلِ يَعْقُوبَ: [يعقوب] is a diptote because it is foreign. ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī claimed that if they said it was another Yaʿqūb, other than Yaʿqūb son of Isḥāq, he would inflect it as triptote; and he said: they did say that he is other than Yaʿqūb son of Isḥāq, peace be upon them both.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: يا زَكَرِيَّا: a singular (mufrad) vocative. اسْمُهُ يَحْيى: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). يحيى is a diptote because it was originally an imperfect verb; it is written with yāʾ to distinguish it from the verb. لَمْ نَجْعَلْ لَهُ مِنْ قَبْلُ سَمِيًّا: we have already mentioned it. It has also been said that its meaning is: We did not command anyone before you to name his son Yaḥyā. «[Translator's note: the source shifts to the second person ("before you") here; translated as written.]»

nahhas-irab:8-8.t:
أَنَّى: in the position of the accusative as an adverbial (ẓarf). وَقَدْ بَلَغْتُ مِنَ الْكِبَرِ عِتِيًّا: Qatāda said:
that is, in age; and the implied form in Arabic is: «an extreme age» (سنّا عتيّا). The original is عتوّا, because it is from the roots with wāw; the wāw was replaced by yāʾ because it is its sister and lighter than it, and because the verses [rhyme] on yāʾ. Whoever read عِتِيًّا [with kasra on the ʿayn] disliked the ḍamma together with the kasra and the yāʾ.

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: قالَ كَذلِكَ قالَ رَبُّكَ: the kāf is in the position of the nominative, i.e. «the matter is thus». هُوَ عَلَيَّ هَيِّنٌ: al-Farrāʾ said: that is, creating him is easy for Me. The people of Medina, the people of Basra and ʿĀṣim read وَقَدْ خَلَقْتُكَ مِنْ قَبْلُ, and the rest of the Kufans read وقد خلقناك. Abū Jaʿfar said: the first reading is closer to the written text (sawād) [of the muṣḥaf].

zajjaj:14-14.t: ﴿وَبَرًّا بِوالِدَيْهِ﴾, that is: "And We made him dutiful (بَرًّا) to his parents."

zajjaj:16-16.t: And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿واذْكُرْ في الكِتابِ مَرْيَمَ إذِ انْتَبَذَتْ مِن أهْلِها مَكانًا شَرْقِيًّا﴾. "اِنْتَبَذَتْ": she withdrew aside. One says "نَبَذْتُ الشَّيْءَ" when you have thrown the thing away. "مَكانًا شَرْقِيًا", that is: towards the east.

zajjaj:17-17.t:
﴿فاتَّخَذَتْ مِن دُونِهِمْ حِجابًا﴾: it is said that she headed towards the place where the sun rises, because she wished to bathe (ghusl) after menstruation. ﴿فَأرْسَلْنا إلَيْها رُوحَنا﴾: by this "جِبْرِيلُ" (Gabriel) ﷺ is meant. It has also been said: "اَلرُّوحُ" (the Spirit) is ʿĪsā (Jesus), because he is a spirit from Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He. Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿إنَّما المَسِيحُ عِيسى ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ وكَلِمَتُهُ ألْقاها إلى مَرْيَمَ ورُوحٌ مِنهُ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 171].
And it has been said: the spirit entered through Maryam's mouth. What shows that Jibrīl — peace be upon him — is the Spirit is His saying: ﴿فَتَمَثَّلَ لَها بَشَرًا سَوِيًّا﴾ "قالَ إنَّما أنا رَسُولُ رَبِّكِ لِيَهَبَ لَكِ غُلامًا زَكِيًّا". Most of the readings have "لِأهَبَ" (that I may give), but "لِيَهَبَ لَكِ" (that He may give you) has also been transmitted, and likewise Abū ʿAmr read: "لِنَهَبَ لَكِ غُلامًا زَكِيًّا". [Translator's note: the attribution to Abū ʿAmr is as it stands in the source; Abū ʿAmr's reading is normally reported as «لِيَهَبَ», with yāʾ, and «لِنَهَبَ» with nūn is not among the well-known readings.]

zajjaj:18-18.t:
﴿قالَتْ إنِّي أعُوذُ بِالرَّحْمَنِ مِنكَ إنْ كُنْتَ تَقِيًّا﴾: its interpretation is: "I seek refuge in Allah from you; so if you are God-fearing, you will take heed from my seeking refuge in Allah from you."
As for whoever read "لِيَهَبَ" with yāʾ, the meaning is: "He sent me so that He may give." And whoever read "لِأهَبَ" — it is by way of reported speech (ḥikāya), with the reported speech carried over to the sense, on the interpretation that he said: "I have been sent to you so that I may give you."

zajjaj:20-20.t: And His saying: ﴿قالَتْ أنّى يَكُونُ لِي غُلامٌ ولَمْ يَمْسَسْنِي بَشَرٌ ولَمْ أكُ بَغِيًّا﴾, that is: "No man has touched me by way of marriage," "وَلَمْ أكُ بَغِيًّا", that is: nor have I been approached outside the bounds of marriage.

zajjaj:21-21.t: ﴿قالَ كَذَلِكِ﴾, that is: "The matter is as I have described to you." ﴿قالَ رَبُّكِ هو عَلَيَّ هَيِّنٌ ولِنَجْعَلَهُ آيَةً لِلنّاسِ ورَحْمَةً مِنّا وكانَ أمْرًا مَقْضِيًّا﴾, that is: and it was a matter that had already preceded in the knowledge of Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — that it would come to pass.

zajjaj:22-22.t: And His saying: ﴿فَحَمَلَتْهُ فانْتَبَذَتْ بِهِ مَكانًا قَصِيًّا﴾. "اِنْتَبَذَتْ بِهِ": she went far away with him. "قَصِيًّا" and "قاصِيًا" have one meaning; its meaning is remoteness.

zajjaj:23-23.t:
And His saying: ﴿فَأجاءَها المَخاضُ إلى جِذْعِ النَّخْلَةِ﴾: its meaning is "it drove her (ألْجَأها)". It is from "جِئْتُ" (I came), and "أجاءَنِي غَيْرِي" (someone else brought me / drove me); and in the same meaning "أشاءَنِي غَيْرِي". Among the proverbs of the Arabs: "شَرٌّ أجاءَكَ إلى مُخَّةِ عُرْقُوبٍ" (an evil drove you to the marrow of a hamstring), and some of them say "أشاءَكَ". Zuhayr said:
؎وَجارٍ سارَ مُعْتَمِدًا إلَيْكم أجاءَتْهُ المَخافَةُ والرَّجاءُ
(And many a protégé who travelled making for you, driven to you by fear and hope.)
There is disagreement about the pregnancy of ʿĪsā — peace be upon him. It has been said that she conceived him and gave birth to him at its [due] time; and it has been said that he was born at eight months, and that this was a sign for him, because no child born at eight months other than him is known to survive.
And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿فَأجاءَها المَخاضُ﴾ indicates that the pregnancy lasted some time; and Allah knows best.
And His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿قالَتْ يا لَيْتَنِي مِتُّ قَبْلَ هَذا﴾: its meaning is: had I been given the choice, before this state, between death and being thrust into this state, I would have chosen death. She knew — may Allah's good pleasure be upon her — that wishing for death before that state would not have benefited her.
And His saying: ﴿وَكُنْتُ نَسْيًا مَنسِيًّا﴾: it is also read "نَسْيًا" with fatḥa on the nūn. It has been said that the meaning of "نَسْيًا" is: a discarded menstrual rag; and it has been said: "نِسْيًا", with kasra, in the sense of "forgotten, so that I am not known". "اَلنِّسْيُ" in the speech of the Arabs is the thing cast aside, to which no attention is paid. Al-Shanfarā said:
؎كَأنَّ لَها في الأرْضِ نِسْيًا تَقُصُّهُ ∗∗∗ عَلى أُمِّها وإنْ تُحَدِّثْكَ تَبْلَتِ
(As though she had something lost on the ground which she traces as she walks, looking downward; and if she speaks to you, she speaks briefly.)
[Translator's note: the source gives the Quranic wording above as «نَسْيًا» and then says "it is also read «نَسْيًا» with fatḥa"; the second reference is evidently to the reading with fatḥa as opposed to the reading «نِسْيًا» with kasra, which is mentioned afterwards.]

zajjaj:24-24.t:
And His saying: ﴿فَناداها مِن تَحْتِها ألا تَحْزَنِي﴾. It is also read "مَن تَحْتَها" (he who was beneath her); the reading with kasra is the more common one. Whoever read "مَن تَحْتَها" meant ʿĪsā — peace be upon him — and the sense of ʿĪsā calling to her would be that Allah makes clear to her the sign in ʿĪsā, and that he informed her that Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — would make a sign for her in the palm tree. Whoever read "مِن تَحْتِها" (from beneath her) meant the angel by it.
﴿قَدْ جَعَلَ رَبُّكِ تَحْتَكِ سَرِيًّا﴾: it is transmitted from al-Ḥasan that he said: it means ʿĪsā; and he said: "By Allah, he was a noble one (سَرِيّ) among men." Then al-Ḥasan learned that among the Arabs there are those who call a stream "سَرِيّ", and he went back to this view. There is no disagreement among the authorities on the language that "اَلسَّرِيُّ" is the stream, like the brook (الجَدْوَل). Labīd said:
؎فَتَوَسَّطا عُرْضَ السَّرِيِّ وصَدَّعا مَسْجُورَةً مُتَجاوِرًا قُلّامُها
(The two of them made for the middle of the stream and split [the reeds of] a brimming pool whose reeds grow close together.)
And Ibn ʿAbbās said: "اَلسَّرِيُّ" is the stream, and he recited:
؎سَلْمٌ تَرى الدّالِيَّ مِنهُ أزْوَرا ∗∗∗ إذا يَعُجُّ في السَّرِيِّ هَرْهَرا
(A well-bucket — you see the water-wheel turning askew from it, when it roars into the stream, gurgling.)

zajjaj:25-25.t:
And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَهُزِّي إلَيْكِ بِجِذْعِ النَّخْلَةِ تُساقِطْ عَلَيْكِ رُطَبًا جَنِيًّا﴾. It is related that it was the trunk of a palm tree that had no crown, and Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — gave it a crown and caused fresh dates to grow on it, and that was in winter.
As for the accusative of "رُطَبًا", Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] said: it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the meaning is: "And shake towards you, by the trunk of the palm tree, fresh dates; they will fall upon you."
"تَساقَطْ عَلَيْكِ" is permissible; "يُساقِطْ عَلَيْكِ" is permissible; "نُساقِطْ عَلَيْكِ" with nūn is permissible; "يَسّاقَطْ" with yāʾ is permissible; "يَتَساقَطْ عَلَيْكِ" is permissible; and "تُساقَطُ عَلَيْكِ", "نُساقِطُ" and "يَسّاقَطُ" with the nominative are permissible; and it is related from al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib. Whoever read "يَسّاقَطْ عَلَيْكِ", the meaning is "يَتَساقَطْ", and the tāʾ was assimilated into the sīn. Whoever read "تَسّاقَطْ", the meaning is also "تَتَساقَطْ", and the yāʾ was assimilated into the sīn [Translator's note: the source says "the yāʾ"; from the form «تَتَساقَطْ» it is the tāʾ that is assimilated], and it was made feminine because the word "النَّخْلَة" (palm tree) is feminine. Whoever read "تَساقَطْ" with tāʾ and without doubling, he dropped one tāʾ of "تَتَساقَطْ" because two tāʾs come together. Whoever read "يُساقِطْ", it is in the sense of "the trunk drops (يُساقِطِ) upon you." Whoever read "نُساقِطُ" with nūn, the meaning is: "We drop upon you, and thereby We make a sign for you."
The grammarians say that "رُطَبًا" is accusative as a tamyīz (specification) when you say "يَسّاقَطْ" or "يَتَساقَطْ"; then the meaning is "the trunk falls in fresh dates." And whoever read "تَساقَطُ", the meaning is: "the palm tree falls in fresh dates."

zajjaj:26-26.t:
And His saying: ﴿فَكُلِي واشْرَبِي وقَرِّي عَيْنًا﴾, that is: "Eat of the fresh dates, drink from the stream (السَّرِيّ), and be comforted (literally: let your eye be cool) by ʿĪsā." One says "قَرِرْتُ بِهِ عَيْنًا، أقَرُّ", with fatḥa on the qāf in the imperfect, and "قَرَرْتُ في المَكانِ، أقِرُّ" (I settled in the place), with kasra on the qāf in the imperfect. "عَيْنًا" is accusative as a tamyīz (specification).
﴿فَإمّا تَرَيِنَّ مِنَ البَشَرِ أحَدًا﴾: without hamza in "تَرَيِنَّ". "تَرْأيِنَّ", with hamza, is also permissible, but no one read it with hamza; it is good and fully eloquent, but it is not permissible in recitation. Likewise His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿إنَّنِي مَعَكُما أسْمَعُ وأرى﴾ [Ṭāhā: 46]: "وَأرْأى" with hamza is permissible, but you do not recite with it — its form being "أرْأى" — because recitation is a sunna (an established practice) that is not departed from. The better form is "أرى", and likewise "تَرَيِنَّ" is better without hamza. The tāʾ is the sign of the feminine, and the original form is "تَرْآيِّنَّ"; the yāʾ was given a vowel because of the meeting of two quiescent letters: the first nūn of the doubled (heavy) nūn and the yāʾ. Likewise you say to a woman: "اِخْشَيِنَّ زَيْدًا" (do fear Zayd).
[Translator's note: the words «بِألِفٍ», «بِغَيْرِ ألِفٍ» in the source are rendered "with/without hamza", since the alif here is the seat of the hamza; the "original form" is given as written in the source.]
﴿فَقُولِي إنِّي نَذَرْتُ لِلرَّحْمَنِ صَوْمًا﴾: the meaning of "صَوْمًا" is silence. One says "نَذَرْتُ النَّذْرَ، أنْذِرُهُ، وأنْذُرُهُ" (I vowed the vow, I vow it), and "نَذِرْتُ بِالقَوْمِ، أنْذَرُ" when I came to know of the people and prepared myself against them.
And His saying: ﴿لَقَدْ جِئْتِ شَيْئًا فَرِيًّا﴾ [Maryam: 27], that is: "a grave thing." One says "فُلانٌ يَفْرِي الفَرِيَّ" when someone does a deed in which he goes to the utmost.

zajjaj:28-28.t:
And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿يا أُخْتَ هارُونَ ما كانَ أبُوكِ امْرَأ سَوْءٍ وما كانَتْ أُمُّكِ بَغِيًّا﴾. There is disagreement about the interpretation of "أُخْتَ هارُونَ" (sister of Hārūn) in this place. We have related in the tafsīr «that the People of the Book said: "How can you say: Maryam was the sister of Hārūn, when there were six hundred years between them?" That was mentioned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: "They used to be named after the prophets and the righteous."», that is: Maryam's brother was named "Hārūn".
And it has been said: they meant "sister of Hārūn" in righteousness and religion. It is related that this Hārūn was a pious man of her people, a righteous one, and that forty thousand people attended his funeral, each one of them named "Hārūn". What has come on this from the Prophet ﷺ is clear.

zajjaj:29-29.t:
And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿فَأشارَتْ إلَيْهِ﴾, that is: when they addressed her, she pointed to him, meaning: "Direct your speech to him." What shows that she pointed to him regarding the speaking is their saying: ﴿كَيْفَ نُكَلِّمُ مَن كانَ في المَهْدِ صَبِيًّا﴾.
In this there are three views. Abū ʿUbayda said: "كانَ" here is redundant (laghw); the meaning is: "How shall we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child?!" — because every man was once a child in the cradle; rather the meaning is: "How shall we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child, the like of whom does not understand and whose tongue does not utter words?"
Some people said: "كانَ" is in the sense of "وَقَعَ" (occurred) and "حَدَثَ" (came about) [i.e. complete kāna]; on their view the meaning is: "How shall we speak to a child who has been brought into being in the cradle?!"
The best of the views is that "مَن" carries the sense of condition and requital (sharṭ and jazāʾ), so that the meaning is: "Whoever is in the cradle as a child" — "صَبِيًّا" being a ḥāl (circumstantial) — "how shall we speak to him?!", just as you say: "Whoever does not hear and does not understand, how shall I address him?!"
It is related that when she gestured towards him, ʿĪsā — peace be upon him — leaned on his left side, pointed with his index finger, and said: ﴿إنِّي عَبْدُ اللَّهِ آتانِيَ الكِتابَ وجَعَلَنِي نَبِيًّا﴾ [Maryam: 30] ﴿وَجَعَلَنِي مُبارَكًا أيْنَ ما كُنْتُ﴾ [Maryam: 31], that is: a teacher of good, ﴿وَأوْصانِي بِالصَّلاةِ والزَّكاةِ ما دُمْتُ حَيًّا﴾ [Maryam: 31]. The meaning of "اَلزَّكاة" here is purity. "ما دُمْتُ حَيًّا": both "دُمْتُ" and "دِمْتُ" are said.

zajjaj:32-32.t: ﴿وَبَرًّا بِوالِدَتِي﴾: "وَبَرًّا" is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to "مُبارَكًا"; the meaning is: "And He made me blessed and dutiful to my mother."

zajjaj:33-33.t:
﴿والسَّلامُ عَلَيَّ يَوْمَ وُلِدْتُ ويَوْمَ أمُوتُ﴾. "اَلسَّلامُ عَلَيَّ": there are several aspects to it. "اَلسَّلامُ" is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of "سَلَّمْتُ، سَلامًا", and its meaning is all-embracing well-being and safety; "اَلسَّلامُ" is also the plural of "سَلامَة"; and "اَلسَّلامُ" is one of the names of Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He.
"سَلامٌ" is among the indefinite nouns with which a sentence may begin (as mubtadaʾ (subject)), because it is a noun that is used frequently. You say "سَلامٌ عَلَيْكَ" and "اَلسَّلامُ عَلَيْكَ". Generic nouns may begin a sentence, because what the indefinite conveys is close to what the definite conveys. You say: "لَبَّيْكَ، وخَيْرٌ بَيْنَ يَدَيْكَ" (At your service, and good is in your hands), and if you wish you say: "والخَيْرُ بَيْنَ يَدَيْكَ". And you say: "اَلسَّلامُ عَلَيْكَ أيُّها النَّبِيُّ" and "سَلامٌ عَلَيْكَ أيُّها النَّبِيُّ". However, since "سَلامٌ" was mentioned before this place without the alif and lām [i.e. without the article, in ﴿وَسَلامٌ عَلَيْهِ يَوْمَ وُلِدَ﴾, 19:15 — Translator's note], it was better that it be repeated the second time with the alif and lām. You say: "سَلامُ عَلَيْكَ أيُّها النَّبِيُّ، اَلسَّلامُ عَلَيْنا وعَلى عِبادِ اللَّهِ الصّالِحِينَ" — this is a good arrangement — and if you wish you say: "سَلامٌ عَلَيْنا وعَلى عِبادِ اللَّهِ الصّالِحِينَ".

zajjaj:34-34.t:
And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿ذَلِكَ عِيسى ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ﴾, that is: that one who said "I am the servant of Allah; He has given me the Book and made me a prophet" is ʿĪsā son of Maryam — not what the Christians say, that he is the son of Allah and that he is a god; Majestic and Mighty is Allah.
And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: "قَوْلُ الحَقِّ" with the nominative; "قَوْلَ الحَقِّ" with the accusative is also permissible. Whoever reads the nominative, the meaning is: "He is the word of truth (هُوَ قَوْلُ الحَقِّ)"; and whoever reads the accusative, the meaning is: "I speak the word of truth (أقُولُ قَوْلَ الحَقِّ)". ﴿الَّذِي فِيهِ يَمْتَرُونَ﴾, that is: they doubt.

zajjaj:35-35.t:
﴿ما كانَ لِلَّهِ أنْ يَتَّخِذَ مِن ولَدٍ﴾: "مِن ولَدٍ" is in the position of the accusative, and the meaning is "that He should take a child (ولَدًا)". "مِن" is emphatic; it indicates [the negation of] the one and of the many. For the speaker may say "ما اتَّخَذْتُ فَرَسًا" (I did not take a horse) meaning "I took more than that", and he may say "ما اتَّخَذْتُ فَرَسَيْنِ، ولا أكْثَرَ" (I did not take two horses, nor more), meaning "I took one horse". But if he says "ما اتَّخَذْتُ مِن فَرَسٍ" (I did not take any horse), he has indicated the negation of the one and of all.
﴿سُبْحانَهُ﴾: its meaning is: declaring Him free of all evil.

zajjaj:37-37.t: And His saying: ﴿فَوَيْلٌ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِن مَشْهَدِ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ﴾: by it the Day of Resurrection is meant.

zajjaj:38-38.t: ﴿أسْمِعْ بِهِمْ وأبْصِرْ يَوْمَ يَأْتُونَنا﴾: the meaning is: "How well they will hear and how well they will see on the Day of Resurrection!", because they will witness, of the resurrection and the command of Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — what makes one hear and see without any exertion of thought and reflection; whereas that to which they are called in this world, of obedience to Allah — Majestic is His majesty — requires thought and reflection of them, so they strayed from it in this world and preferred amusement and caprice. So Allah the Exalted said: ﴿لَكِنِ الظّالِمُونَ اليَوْمَ في ضَلالٍ مُبِينٍ﴾.

zajjaj:39-39.t: And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَأنْذِرْهم يَوْمَ الحَسْرَةِ إذْ قُضِيَ الأمْرُ وهم في غَفْلَةٍ﴾. "يَوْمُ الحَسْرَةِ" (the Day of Regret) is the Day of Resurrection. It is related in the tafsīr «that when the Day of Resurrection comes, and the people of Paradise have settled in Paradise and the people of the Fire in the Fire, death will be brought in the form of a white-and-black ram and shown to the people of the Fire, and they will crane their necks towards it. It will be said: "Do you recognise this?" They will say: "Yes." It will be said: "This is death." Then it will be slaughtered, and it will be proclaimed: "O people of the Fire, eternity, with no death after it." And likewise it will be proclaimed: "O people of Paradise, eternity, with no death after it."» ﴿وَهم في غَفْلَةٍ﴾, that is: they are, in this world, in heedlessness.

zajjaj:41-41.t: ﴿واذْكُرْ في الكِتابِ إبْراهِيمَ إنَّهُ كانَ صِدِّيقًا نَبِيًّا﴾, that is: mention in the Book that has been sent down to you — namely the Quran — the story of Ibrāhīm and his account. "اَلصِّدِّيقُ" is a noun of intensiveness in truthfulness. Everyone who affirms the oneness of Allah and His prophets, and acts according to what he affirms, is called "صِدِّيقٌ"; and from this Abū Bakr was named al-Ṣiddīq.

zajjaj:42-42.t:
And His saying: ﴿إذْ قالَ لأبِيهِ يا أبَتِ لِمَ تَعْبُدُ﴾: the pause on it is "يا أبَهْ", with hāʾ. The Arabs say in the vocative "يا أبَةِ" and "يا أُمَّةِ", but they do not say "قالَ أبَتِي كَذا" nor "قالَتْ أُمَّتِي كَذا". Al-Khalīl and Sībawayh held that it is like their saying "يا عَمَّةَ" and "يا خالَةَ", and that "أبَةِ" is for masculine and feminine, as though you say to the masculine "أبَةِ", and to the feminine [Translator's note: the sentence breaks off thus in the source]. The proof that the mother has a share in "fatherhood" is that one says "أبَوانِ" (the two parents, literally "the two fathers"). Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿وَوَرِثَهُ أبَواهُ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 11].
And he held that it is like their saying "رَجُلٌ رَبْعَةٌ" (a man of medium build) and "غُلامٌ يَفَعَةٌ" (a youth near puberty) [i.e. masculine nouns with the feminine ending], and that the hāʾ in "أبَةِ" is a substitute for the yāʾ of the first-person possessive in "يا أبِي" and "يا أُمِّي"; and he did not say "يا أبَتِي" nor "يا أُمَّتِي". For that reason the hāʾ does not occur outside the vocative, because dropping the yāʾ happens frequently in the vocative: you say "يا أبِ لا تَفْعَلْ" (O my father, do not do it), but you do not say "قالَ أبِ كَذا وكَذا" meaning "قالَ أبِي" (my father said). And the feminine may be described with a masculine form, as in their saying "اِمْرَأةٌ طالِقٌ، وطاهِرٌ" (a divorced woman, a ritually pure woman); and one says "ثَلاثَةُ أنْفُسٍ" (three souls), though "اَلنَّفْسُ" is feminine — the masculine was named by it. This is an exhaustive and accessible explanation.

zajjaj:43-43.t:
And His saying: ﴿إنِّي قَدْ جاءَنِي مِنَ العِلْمِ ما لَمْ يَأْتِكَ﴾ indicates that revelation had already come to him. And the meaning of ﴿صِراطًا سَوِيًّا﴾ is: a straight path.
And His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿يا أبَتِ لا تَعْبُدِ الشَّيْطانَ إنَّ الشَّيْطانَ كانَ لِلرَّحْمَنِ عَصِيًّا﴾ [Maryam: 44]: the meaning of worshipping Satan — and Allah knows best — is obeying him in the disbelief and sins that he makes seem attractive.

zajjaj:44-44.t:
﴿يا أبَتِ لا تَعْبُدِ الشَّيْطانَ﴾: whoever reads it with fatḥa [يا أبَتَ] has dropped the alif that was substituted for the yāʾ of the first-person possessive; he intended "يا أبَتا", the alif being a substitute (badal) for the yāʾ of the possessive, except that it must be dropped, since it is a substitute for a yāʾ that is dropped.
And His saying: ﴿لِمَ تَعْبُدُ ما لا يَسْمَعُ ولا يُبْصِرُ ولا يُغْنِي عَنْكَ شَيْئًا﴾ [Maryam: 42] means the idol.

zajjaj:46-46.t: And His saying: ﴿لأرْجُمَنَّكَ﴾: its meaning is "I will surely revile you." One says "فُلانٌ يَرْمِي فُلانًا" (so-and-so pelts so-and-so) and "يَرْجُمُ فُلانًا" (stones so-and-so), meaning: he reviles him. Likewise His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿والَّذِينَ يَرْمُونَ المُحْصَناتِ﴾ [al-Nūr: 4]; its meaning is "they revile them." It is also possible that "لَأرْجُمَنَّكَ" means "I will surely kill you by stoning"; but what the tafsīr holds is that rajm here is reviling.

zajjaj:47-47.t: And His saying: ﴿إنَّهُ كانَ بِي حَفِيًّا﴾: its meaning is: kind (لَطِيفًا). One says "قَدْ تَحَفّى فُلانٌ بِفُلانٍ" and "حَفِيَ فُلانٌ بِفُلانٍ، حَفْوَةً" when he treats him dutifully and kindly.

zajjaj:50-50.t: And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَجَعَلْنا لَهم لِسانَ صِدْقٍ عَلِيًّا﴾, that is: We left for them a good praise [among later generations]; and likewise His saying: ﴿واجْعَلْ لِي لِسانَ صِدْقٍ في الآخِرِينَ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 84].

zajjaj:51-51.t: And His saying: ﴿واذْكُرْ في الكِتابِ مُوسى إنَّهُ كانَ مُخْلَصًا﴾ — and "مُخْلِصًا"; both are read. "اَلْمُخْلَصُ", with fatḥa on the lām, is the one whom Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — has made pure (أخْلَصَهُ), that is: made him chosen, pure of defilement. "اَلْمُخْلِصُ", with kasra on the lām, is the one who has affirmed the oneness of Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — and made himself sincere (pure) in obedience to Allah, undefiled.

zajjaj:52-52.t: And His saying: ﴿وَقَرَّبْناهُ نَجِيًّا﴾: its meaning is: as one in intimate converse (مُناجِيًا). It has come in the tafsīr that Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — brought him near until he heard the scratching of the pen with which the Torah was written. And it is possible — and Allah knows best — that it is like ﴿وَكَلَّمَ اللَّهُ مُوسى تَكْلِيمًا﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 164], that is: He brought him near in rank until he heard the intimate address of Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — which is the speech of Allah.

zajjaj:53-53.t: And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَوَهَبْنا لَهُ مِن رَحْمَتِنا أخاهُ هارُونَ نَبِيًّا﴾: "هارُونُ" is a diptote (it does not take full declension) when definite, because it is a foreign name and it is definite.

zajjaj:55-55.t:
And His saying — Glorified is He —: ﴿وَكانَ يَأْمُرُ أهْلَهُ بِالصَّلاةِ والزَّكاةِ﴾: his "people" (أهْلُهُ) are his whole community, whether related to him by kinship or not; and likewise the "people" of every prophet are his community.
﴿وَكانَ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِ مَرْضِيًّا﴾: its original form is "مَرْضُوًّا", which is permissible in the language but not permissible in the Quran, because it contradicts the muṣḥaf. Al-Khalīl, Sībawayh and all the Basrans say "فُلانٌ مَرْضُوٌّ، ومَرْضِيٌّ" (so-and-so is well-pleasing), and "أرْضٌ مَسْنُوَّةٌ، ومَسْنِيَّةٌ" (irrigated land) when it has been watered by water-wheels (السَّوانِي) or by rain. The original letter is wāw, but — according to al-Khalīl — it was changed because it is final, preceded by a quiescent wāw, which is not a firm barrier; so it is as if it were "مَفْعُلٌ", with ḍamma on the ʿayn, and "مَفْعُلٌ" from roots with wāw is changed to "مَفْعِلٌ", because in nouns a wāw does not occur finally preceded by a voweled letter.
As for those other than Sībawayh and the Basrans, they have two views on it. Some of them said: since its verb is "رَضِيتُ", it passed from wāw to yāʾ, and it became "مَرْضِيًّا". And it has been said: some Arabs say in the dual of "رِضًى" both "رِضَيانِ" and "رِضَوانِ"; whoever says "رِضَيانِ" can only say "مَرَضِيٌّ", and whoever says "رِضَوانِ" in the dual may say both "فُلانٌ مَرْضُوٌّ" and "مَرَضِيٌّ".
[Translator's note: «مَرَضِيٌّ» is vocalised thus in the source; «مَرْضِيٌّ» is evidently intended.]

zajjaj:57-57.t:
And His saying — Glorified is He —: ﴿وَرَفَعْناهُ مَكانًا عَلِيًّا﴾: it has come in the tafsīr that he was raised to the fourth heaven. It has also come in the tafsīr that he asked the Angel of Death — until he asked Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — that he raise him; so he was brought into the Fire, then brought out, then brought into Paradise. Then he was told to come out, and he said: "Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — has said: ﴿وَإنْ مِنكم إلا وارِدُها﴾ [Maryam: 71], and He said about the people of Paradise: ﴿وَما هم مِنها بِمُخْرَجِينَ﴾ [al-Ḥijr: 48]." So Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — settled him in Paradise. This argument is only found in the Quran — and Allah knows best.
It is possible that Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — had informed Idrīs, before He sent down the Quran, that all creatures would come to the Fire and that they [the believers] would abide forever in the Gardens, and the Quran came in agreement with what Idrīs had been taught. It has come in the tafsīr that he was raised as ʿĪsā was raised. And it is possible — and Allah knows best — that His saying ﴿وَرَفَعْناهُ مَكانًا عَلِيًّا﴾ means: in prophethood and knowledge.
[Translator's note: «حَتّى سَألَ اللَّهَ أنْ رَفَعَهُ» is as worded in the source; the sense is that the Angel of Death asked Allah, at Idrīs's request, to raise him.]

zajjaj:58-58.t: And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿خَرُّوا سُجَّدًا وبُكِيًّا﴾: Allah — Glorified is He — has made clear that the prophets, when they heard the signs of Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — prostrated and wept out of fear of Allah. "بُكِيًّا" is the plural of "باكٍ" (weeping), like "شاهِدٌ" and "شُهُودٌ", and "قاعِدٌ" and "قُعُودٌ". "سُجَّدًا" is an anticipated ḥāl (circumstantial; ḥāl muqaddara); the meaning is "they fell down intending prostration", because a person, while falling down, is not [yet] prostrating. "سُجَّدًا" is accusative as a ḥāl. Whoever says that "بُكِيًّا" here is a maṣdar (verbal noun) is mistaken, because "سُجَّدًا" is the plural of "ساجِدٌ", and "بُكِيًّا" is conjoined to it. One says "بَكى، بُكاءً، وبُكِيًّا" (he wept, weeping).

zajjaj:59-59.t:
And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿فَخَلَفَ مِن بَعْدِهِمْ خَلْفٌ أضاعُوا الصَّلاةَ﴾: for badness one says "خَلْفٌ", with the lām quiescent — you say "خَلْفُ سُوءٍ" (an evil succession) — and for goodness "خَلَفُ صِدْقٍ" (a true successor), with fatḥa on the lām. "خَلَفٌ" with fatḥa on the lām is also sometimes said for badness, and with the lām quiescent for goodness; but the first usage is better.
﴿أضاعُوا الصَّلاةَ واتَّبَعُوا الشَّهَواتِ﴾: it has come in the tafsīr that they prayed it outside its time; and it has been said: they neglected it and abandoned it altogether. This is the more likely, because it indicates that the disbelievers are meant by it, and the proof of that is His saying: ﴿إلا مَن تابَ وآمَنَ﴾ [Maryam: 60].
And His saying: ﴿فَسَوْفَ يَلْقَوْنَ غَيًّا﴾, that is: they will meet the requital of error (الغَيّ), as He — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿وَمَن يَفْعَلْ ذَلِكَ يَلْقَ أثامًا﴾ [al-Furqān: 68], that is: the requital of sin. It has come in the tafsīr that "غَيًّا" is a valley in Hell; and it has been said: a river in Hell. It is possible that it is a river prepared for those in error (الغاوِين), and so it was called "غَيًّا".

zajjaj:60-60.t: And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿إلا مَن تابَ وآمَنَ﴾: "مَن" is in the position of the accusative, that is: "they will meet the punishment, except those who repent." It may also be accusative as an exception from something other than the first [i.e. a disconnected exception], the meaning being: "But whoever repents and believes…" ﴿فَأُولَئِكَ يَدْخُلُونَ الجَنَّةَ﴾: it is also read "يُدْخَلُونَ الجَنَّةَ" (they will be admitted into the Garden), passive.

zajjaj:61-61.t:
And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿جَنّاتِ عَدْنٍ﴾: the nominative and the accusative are both permissible. The nominative is in the sense of "They are Gardens of ʿAdn (هِيَ جَنّاتُ عَدْنٍ)", and the accusative in the sense of "They will enter Gardens of ʿAdn (يَدْخُلُونَ جَنّاتِ عَدْنٍ)". "عَدْنٍ" means "permanent residence"; one says "عَدَنَ بِالمَكانِ" when he resides in the place.
And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿إنَّهُ كانَ وعْدُهُ مَأْتِيًّا﴾: "مَأْتِيًّا" is a passive participle (mafʿūl) from "اَلْإتْيانُ" (coming), because everything that has reached you, you have reached it, and everything that has come to you, you have come to it. One says "وَصَلْتُ إلى خَيْرِ فُلانٍ، ووَصَلَ إلَيَّ خَيْرُ فُلانٍ" (I reached so-and-so's bounty, and so-and-so's bounty reached me) and "أتَيْتُ خَيْرَ فُلانٍ، وأتانِي خَيْرُ فُلانٍ" (I came to so-and-so's bounty, and so-and-so's bounty came to me). So this is in the sense of "I came to so-and-so's bounty."

zajjaj:62-62.t:
And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿لا يَسْمَعُونَ فِيها لَغْوًا إلا سَلامًا﴾: "اَللَّغْوُ" is speech that is discarded and in which there is sin. "سَلامًا" is a noun comprehending all good and containing safety; so the meaning is that the people of Paradise hear only what keeps them safe.
And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَلَهم رِزْقُهم فِيها بُكْرَةً وعَشِيًّا﴾: it has been said: there is no morning or evening there, but they were addressed with what they understand in this world; so the meaning is: "They have their provision in the measure of what lies between morning and evening." It has also come in the tafsīr that its meaning is: they have their provision there at every hour. And if it is said "in the measure of morning and evening", then what is apportioned at that time is the measure of what they want at every hour, until the time that follows it comes.

zajjaj:64-64.t:
And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَما نَتَنَـزَّلُ إلا بِأمْرِ رَبِّكَ﴾: it is related «that Jibrīl — peace be upon him — was slow in coming to the Prophet ﷺ with revelation, and when Jibrīl came to him he — peace be upon him — said: "You did not visit us until I longed for you." So he said: ﴿وَما نَتَنَـزَّلُ إلا بِأمْرِ رَبِّكَ﴾».
And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿لَهُ ما بَيْنَ أيْدِينا وما خَلْفَنا وما بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ﴾: "ما بَيْنَ أيْدِينا" (what is before us) is the matter of the Hereafter, reward and punishment; "وَما خَلْفَنا" (and what is behind us) is all that has passed of the affair of this world; "وَما بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ" (and what is between that) is what will be from us from this time until the Day of Resurrection. It has come in the tafsīr regarding "وَما بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ": it has been said, what is between the two blasts [of the Trumpet].
And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَما كانَ رَبُّكَ نَسِيًّا﴾, that is: Allah — Majestic and Exalted is He — knows what has been, what will be and what is coming to be; He preserves that — Mighty and Majestic is He — and forgets nothing of it. And it is possible — and Allah knows best — that it means: your Lord has not forgotten you, even if revelation has been delayed for you.

zajjaj:65-65.t:
And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿رَبُّ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ وما بَيْنَهُما﴾, that is: He is their Owner, and Knower of them and of what is in them.
And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿هَلْ تَعْلَمُ لَهُ سَمِيًّا﴾: it has come in the tafsīr: Do you know any like unto Him? It has also come: none has been named "اَلرَّحْمَنُ" except Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He. Its interpretation — and Allah knows best — is: Do you know any namesake of His who deserves to be called "Creator", "All-Powerful" and "Knower of what has been and what will be"? That is only among the attributes of Allah the Exalted.

zajjaj:66-66.t: And His saying: ﴿وَيَقُولُ الإنْسانُ أإذا ما مِتُّ لَسَوْفَ أُخْرَجُ حَيًّا﴾: by this is meant specifically the disbeliever who does not believe in the Unseen. Both "مُتُّ" and "مِتُّ" [are said].

zajjaj:67-67.t: And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿أوَلا يَذْكُرُ الإنْسانُ﴾ — it is also read "أوَلا يَذَّكَّرُ" — with the light and the doubled form. ﴿أنّا خَلَقْناهُ مِن قَبْلُ ولَمْ يَكُ شَيْئًا﴾: Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — made known that bringing creation back is like originating their creation. This is as He said: ﴿وَضَرَبَ لَنا مَثَلا ونَسِيَ خَلْقَهُ﴾ [Yā Sīn: 78] — the verse — and the answer was: ﴿قُلْ يُحْيِيها الَّذِي أنْشَأها أوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ﴾ [Yā Sīn: 79].

zajjaj:68-68.t:
And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿فَوَرَبِّكَ لَنَحْشُرَنَّهم والشَّياطِينَ﴾, that is: "By your Lord, We shall surely resurrect them and gather them together with the devils who led them astray." ﴿ثُمَّ لَنُحْضِرَنَّهم حَوْلَ جَهَنَّمَ جِثِيًّا﴾ — and "جُثِيًّا"; with ḍamma and kasra, both. The meaning of "جِثِيًّا" is: on their knees, unable to stand because of what they are in. "جُثِيٌّ" is the plural of "جاثٍ" (kneeling): "جاثٍ" and "جُثِيٌّ" are like "قاعِدٌ" and "قُعُودٌ", and "بارِكٌ" and "بُرُوكٌ".
The original is ḍamma on the jīm; kasra is permissible to harmonise with the kasra [before] the yāʾ. "جِثِيًّا" is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

zajjaj:69-69.t:
And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿ثُمَّ لَنَنْـزِعَنَّ مِن كُلِّ شِيعَةٍ أيُّهم أشَدُّ عَلى الرَّحْمَنِ عِتِيًّا﴾ — and "عُتِيًّا"; with kasra and ḍamma. Its meaning is: "We shall surely draw out from every community and every sect the most insolent, then the next most insolent of them" — as though the punishment begins with the most severe of them in insolence, then the one who follows him.
As for the nominative of "أيُّهُمْ", it is the reading. "أيَّهُمْ" in the accusative is also permissible; Sībawayh reported it, and Sībawayh mentioned that Hārūn al-Aʿwar, the Quran reader, read it so. Regarding its nominative there are three views.
Sībawayh said, on the authority of Yūnus: His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He — "لَنَنْزِعَنَّ" is suspended (muʿallaqa); it has governed nothing. So it is as if Yūnus's view is: "Then We shall surely draw out from every community" — then He began anew and said: "Which of them was most severe in insolence against the All-Merciful?!"
As for al-Khalīl, Sībawayh reported from him that it is in the sense of "those of whom it is said: which of them was most severe in insolence against the All-Merciful?!" In his view its like is the poet's saying:
؎وَلَقَدْ أبِيتُ مِنَ الفَتاةِ بِمَنزِلٍ فَأبِيتُ لا حَرِجٌ ولا مَحْرُومُ
(I have spent the night in a position with the young woman such that I pass the night neither guilty nor deprived.)
The meaning is: "I pass the night in the position of one of whom it is said: he is neither guilty nor deprived."
And Sībawayh said: "أيُّهُمْ" is indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, because it differs from its sisters and the [mubtadaʾ of the] nominal sentence is used with it [omitted]: you say "اِضْرِبْ أيُّهم أفْضَلُ" (strike whichever of them is best), meaning "أيَّهم هو أفْضَلُ", and the usage is good thus, with "هُوَ" omitted; whereas "اِضْرِبْ مَن أفْضَلُ" is not good until you say "مَن هو أفْضَلُ", and "كُلْ ما أطْيَبُ" is not good until you say "كُلْ ما هو أطْيَبُ". So it differs from "مَن", "ما" and "اَلَّذِي" — since you also do not say "خُذِ الَّذِي أفْضَلُ" until you say "هُوَ أفْضَلُ". He said: since it differs in this way, it was made indeclinable on the ḍamma when it is in a genitive construct (iḍāfa). The accusative is good even though you have omitted "هُوَ", because "هُوَ" may be omitted; and it has been read: "تَمامًا عَلى الَّذِي أحْسَنُ وتَفْصِيلًا" in the sense of "اَلَّذِي هو أحْسَنُ".
[Translator's note: the source prints «اِضْرِبْ لَأيُّهم أفْضَلُ»; the lām appears to be a corruption, and the example is rendered without it.]
Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: What I hold is that the correct view in this is al-Khalīl's, and it agrees with the tafsīr, because al-Khalīl's doctrine — or his interpretation — of His saying, Exalted is He, is: "Then We shall surely draw out from every community the one about whom, because of his insolence, it is said: which of these is most severe in insolence?!" So that is applied to the most severe, then the next most severe; and Allah knows best.

zajjaj:70-70.t: And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿ثُمَّ لَنَحْنُ أعْلَمُ بِالَّذِينَ هم أوْلى بِها صِلِيًّا﴾ — and "صُلِيًّا"; with ḍamma and kasra, as we have explained. "صِلِيًّا" is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) [Translator's note: so in the source; it is more commonly parsed as a tamyīz], that is: "Then We know best those who are most severe in insolence against the All-Merciful, so they are most deserving of burning in it."

zajjaj:71-71.t:
﴿وَإنْ مِنكم إلا وارِدُها كانَ عَلى رَبِّكَ حَتْمًا مَقْضِيًّا﴾: this is a verse about which there is much disagreement of interpretation in the tafsīr. Many people said: all creatures will come to the Fire; the God-fearing will be saved and the wrongdoer left behind, and all of them will enter it. One of them said: "We know of the coming down to it, but we do not know of the coming away from it." The argument of whoever holds this view is that mention had been made of the disbelievers, when He said: ﴿ثُمَّ لَنَنْـزِعَنَّ مِن كُلِّ شِيعَةٍ أيُّهم أشَدُّ﴾ [Maryam: 69], and then He said afterwards: ﴿وَإنْ مِنكم إلا وارِدُها﴾; so it is as though, in the arrangement of that discourse, it is general. And the proof of whoever holds this view is also
[Translator's note: the entry breaks off here in the source; the discussion continues under the next verse (19:72).]

zajjaj:72-72.t:
His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ نُنَجِّي الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا ونَذَرُ الظّالِمِينَ﴾ — and He did not say "and We will admit the wrongdoers"; it is as though "نَذَرُ" and "نَتْرُكُ" (We leave) are used for a thing that is already present in its place.
Some people said: this refers specifically to the polytheists, and in this they argued that some read: "وَإنْ مِنهم إلّا وارِدُها" (there is none of them but will come to it). On the doctrine of these people, "ثُمَّ نُنَجِّي الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا" would mean: "We bring out the God-fearing from among the whole of those whom We admit into the Fire."
Others said: all creatures will come to it, and it will be coolness and safety for the believer; then he will be brought out of it and admitted into Paradise, and he will know the excellence of the blessing from what he witnesses there of the people of punishment and what he saw there of the people of the Fire.
Ibn Masʿūd, al-Ḥasan and Qatāda said: "Coming to it is not entering it." Their argument for this is very good from several angles. One of them is that the Arabs say "وَرَدْتُ ماءَ كَذا" (I came to such-and-such water) without having entered it. And Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿وَلَمّا ورَدَ ماءَ مَدْيَنَ وجَدَ عَلَيْهِ أُمَّةً مِنَ النّاسِ يَسْقُونَ﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 23]. And when you reach a town without entering it you say: "I have come to (وَرَدْتُ) such-and-such a town."
Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: the decisive proof for this view is what Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ سَبَقَتْ لَهم مِنّا الحُسْنى أُولَئِكَ عَنْها مُبْعَدُونَ﴾ [al-Anbiyāʾ: 101] ﴿لا يَسْمَعُونَ حَسِيسَها﴾ [al-Anbiyāʾ: 102]. This — and Allah knows best — is proof that the people of the best reward do not enter the Fire.
In the language, "وَرَدْتُ بَلَدَ كَذا وكَذا" is said when you have come within sight of it, whether you entered it or not. Zuhayr said:
؎فَلَمّا ورَدْنَ الماءَ زُرْقًا جِمامُهُ وضَعْنَ عِصِيَّ الحاضِرِ المُتَخَيِّمِ
(When they [the women] came to the water, its gathered pools clear blue, they set down their staffs like a settled camper pitching his tent.)
The meaning is: "they reached the water", that is, they stayed by it; so "coming" (وُرُود) here, by consensus, is not entering. These, then, are the transmitted views on this verse; and Allah knows best.

zajjaj:73-73.t: And His saying: ﴿وَأحْسَنُ نَدِيًّا﴾: its meaning is: an assembly (مَجْلِسًا).

zajjaj:74-74.t:
And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿أحْسَنُ أثاثًا ورِئْيًا﴾: there are four forms in it: "رِئْيًا", with a hamza before the yāʾ and the rāʾ undotted; "وَرِيًّا", with doubling, with a doubled yāʾ; and "وَزِيًّا", with the dotted zāy. It has been read in these three forms. A fourth form is permissible which has not been read: with a yāʾ followed by a hamza, "وَرِيئًا".
As for "رِئْيًا", with a hamza before the yāʾ, the meaning in it is: "They were better in furnishings (أثاثًا) — that is, goods — and in appearance (رِئْيًا) — that is, outward look", from "رَأيْتُ" (I saw). Whoever reads without hamza has two interpretations: in the sense of the first, with the hamza dropped; or in the sense that their appearance is well-watered (مُرْتَوٍ) with comfort, as though the bliss is evident in them. Whoever reads "زِيًّا", its meaning is that their attire (زِيّ) was fine, meaning their outward form. The poet said:
؎أشاقَتْكَ الظَّعائِنُ يَوْمَ بانُوا بِذِي الرِّئْيِ الجَمِيلِ مِنَ الأثاثِ
(Did the women in their litters fill you with longing on the day they departed, with their beautiful-looking furnishings?)
"أحْسَنُ أثاثًا وزِيًّا" was put in the accusative with the intention of specification (tafsīr, i.e. tamyīz); the meaning is: "How many a generation We destroyed before them who were better than them in furnishings, and better than them in attire."
Whoever reads "رِيئًا", it is in the sense of "رِئْيًا", transposed (maqlūb), because among the Arabs there are those who say "قَدْ راءَنِي زَيْدٌ" (Zayd saw me), and you say "قَدْ رَآنِي" in this sense. The poet Kuthayyir said:
؎وَكُلُّ خَلِيلٍ راءَنِي فَهْوَ قائِلٌ ∗∗∗ مِنَ اجْلِكَ هَذا هامَةُ اليَوْمِ أوْ غَدِ
(And every friend who sees me says: because of you, this man is a ghost (a dead man) today or tomorrow.)

zajjaj:75-75.t:
And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿قُلْ مَن كانَ في الضَّلالَةِ فَلْيَمْدُدْ لَهُ الرَّحْمَنُ مَدًّا﴾: this is the wording of a command in the sense of a statement (khabar). Its interpretation is that Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — has made the requital of his error that He leaves him in it and extends him in it, as He — Majestic and Mighty is He — said: ﴿مَن يُضْلِلِ اللَّهُ فَلا هادِيَ لَهُ ويَذَرُهم في طُغْيانِهِمْ يَعْمَهُونَ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 186]. However, the wording of the command emphasises the sense of the statement, as though by the wording of the command the speaker means to bind himself, as if he were saying: "I do that and I command myself to do it." So if someone says "مَن رَآنِي فَلْأُكْرِمْهُ" (whoever sees me, let me honour him), it is more binding than his saying "أُكْرِمُهُ" (I honour him); it is as if he said: "Whoever visits me, I command myself to honour him and bind myself to it."
And His saying: ﴿إمّا العَذابَ وإمّا السّاعَةَ﴾: "اَلْعَذابَ" and "اَلسّاعَةَ" are both accusative as a badal (substitute) for "ما يُوعَدُونَ" (what they are promised); the meaning is: "until, when they see the punishment or they see the Hour…" The punishment here is what they were promised of the victory of the believers over them, for they will punish them by killing and captivity. And "اَلسّاعَةُ" (the Hour) refers to the Day of Resurrection and what they were promised in it of eternity in the Fire. ﴿فَسَيَعْلَمُونَ مَن هو شَرٌّ مَكانًا وأضْعَفُ جُنْدًا﴾, that is: they will know, through the victory and the killing, that they are weaker in troops than the troops of the Prophet ﷺ and the Muslims; and they will know, through their place in Hell and the place of the believers in Paradise, who is worse in position.

zajjaj:76-76.t:
And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَيَزِيدُ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ اهْتَدَوْا هُدًى﴾: it has been said: by the abrogating and the abrogated, such as what there was regarding the fast of Ramaḍān — that it was permissible for one able to fast to feed a poor person and not fast; then that was abrogated by making fasting obligatory. And it is possible that ﴿وَيَزِيدُ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ اهْتَدَوْا هُدًى﴾ means: He makes their reward that He increases them in guidance in their certainty, just as Allah leads the transgressor astray because of his transgression.
And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿والباقِياتُ الصّالِحاتُ خَيْرٌ عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ ثَوابًا﴾: its meaning is: righteous deeds, the first of which is affirming the oneness of Allah, namely the testimony that there is no god but Allah.

zajjaj:77-77.t:
And His saying: ﴿أفَرَأيْتَ الَّذِي كَفَرَ بِآياتِنا وقالَ لأُوتَيَنَّ مالا ووَلَدًا﴾ — it is also read "وَوُلْدًا". Whoever reads "وُلْدًا" with ḍamma, it is on one of two aspects: as the plural of "وَلَدٌ" — one says "وَلَدٌ" and "وُلْدٌ" like "أسَدٌ" and "أُسْدٌ" (lion, lions); or "اَلْوُلْدُ" may be in the sense of "اَلْوَلَدُ" — and "الوَلَدُ" serves for the singular and the plural — so that "اَلْوُلْدُ" and "اَلْوَلَدُ" have one meaning, like "اَلْعُرْبُ" and "اَلْعَرَبُ" (the Arabs), and "اَلْعُجْمُ" and "اَلْعَجَمُ" (the non-Arabs).
It has come in the tafsīr that al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil is meant by it. It is related that Khabbāb said: "I was a qayn in the Jāhiliyya" — the qayn is the one who repairs spearheads, and the blacksmith is called "qayn" — he said: "Al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil owed me a debt, and he put me off in paying it, and said: I will not pay it to you until you disbelieve in Muḥammad ﷺ." Khabbāb said: "I will not disbelieve in Muḥammad until you die and are resurrected." He said: "When I die and then am resurrected, I will be given wealth and children, and I will pay you from what I am given" — saying that in mockery. So Allah — Glorified is He — said: ﴿أطَّلَعَ الغَيْبَ أمِ اتَّخَذَ عِنْدَ الرَّحْمَنِ عَهْدًا﴾ [Maryam: 78], that is: "Did he know that as part of the Unseen, or was he given a covenant?!" He is like the one who said: ﴿وَلَئِنْ رُدِدْتُ إلى رَبِّي لأجِدَنَّ خَيْرًا مِنها مُنْقَلَبًا﴾ [al-Kahf: 36].

zajjaj:79-79.t: ﴿كَلا﴾: a word of deterrence and warning (radʿ and tanbīh), that is: this is something from which one should be deterred, and attention is drawn to the aspect of error in it. ﴿سَنَكْتُبُ ما يَقُولُ﴾, that is: We shall record it against him.

zajjaj:80-80.t: ﴿وَنَرِثُهُ ما يَقُولُ ويَأْتِينا فَرْدًا﴾, that is: We shall give the wealth and the children to someone else and strip him of that, and he will come to Us alone.

zajjaj:81-81.t: And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿لِيَكُونُوا لَهم عِزًّا﴾, that is: helpers.

zajjaj:82-82.t: And His saying: ﴿وَيَكُونُونَ عَلَيْهِمْ ضِدًّا﴾, that is: they will become helpers against them.

zajjaj:83-83.t: And His saying: ﴿ألَمْ تَرَ أنّا أرْسَلْنا الشَّياطِينَ عَلى الكافِرِينَ تَؤُزُّهم أزًّا﴾: in His saying "أرْسَلْنا" there are two aspects. One of them: "We left the devils and them to each other, and did not protect them from accepting from them." Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: the second aspect — and it is the preferred one — is that they were sent against them and assigned to them because of their disbelief, as He — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿وَمَن يَعْشُ عَنْ ذِكْرِ الرَّحْمَنِ نُقَيِّضْ لَهُ شَيْطانًا فَهو لَهُ قَرِينٌ﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 36]. The meaning of "تَؤُزُّهم أزًّا" is: they stir them up until they commit sins, with a vehement stirring; and this indicates the soundness of [the interpretation as] sending and assigning. The meaning of sending (al-irsāl) here is giving power over (al-taslīṭ); one says "قَدْ أرْسَلْتُ فُلانًا عَلى فُلانٍ" when you have given him power over him, as He said: ﴿إنَّ عِبادِي لَيْسَ لَكَ عَلَيْهِمْ سُلْطانٌ إلا مَنِ اتَّبَعَكَ مِنَ الغاوِينَ﴾ [al-Ḥijr: 42]. So Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — made known that whoever follows him, he [Satan] is given power over him.

zajjaj:85-85.t: And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿يَوْمَ نَحْشُرُ المُتَّقِينَ إلى الرَّحْمَنِ وفْدًا﴾: the meaning of "اَلْوَفْدُ" is: honoured riders. ﴿وَنَسُوقُ المُجْرِمِينَ إلى جَهَنَّمَ وِرْدًا﴾ [Maryam: 86]: on foot, thirsty.

zajjaj:87-87.t: And His saying: ﴿لا يَمْلِكُونَ الشَّفاعَةَ إلا مَنِ اتَّخَذَ عِنْدَ الرَّحْمَنِ عَهْدًا﴾: "مَن" may be in the position of the nominative or in the position of the accusative. As for the nominative, it is as a badal (substitute) for the wāw and nūn [of "يَمْلِكُونَ"], and the meaning is: "None will possess intercession except whoever has taken a covenant with the All-Merciful." The covenant (اَلْعَهْدُ) here is affirming the oneness of Allah — exalted is His praise — and faith in Him. The accusative is as an exception not from the first [i.e. a disconnected exception], on the sense: "The criminals do not possess intercession," then He said "except whoever has taken a covenant with the All-Merciful", in the sense of "but whoever has taken a covenant with the All-Merciful does possess intercession."

zajjaj:89-89.t: And His saying: ﴿لَقَدْ جِئْتُمْ شَيْئًا إدًّا﴾ — it is also read "أدًّا" with fatḥa — its meaning is: "a monstrous thing of disbelief." There is another dialectal form in it which I do not know to have been read, namely "شَيْئًا آدًّا", on the pattern of "رادًّا" and "مادًّا". The meaning of all of it is: "You have brought a monstrous thing."

zajjaj:96-96.t: And His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وعَمِلُوا الصّالِحاتِ سَيَجْعَلُ لَهُمُ الرَّحْمَنُ وُدًّا﴾, that is: "love in the hearts of the believers."

zajjaj:97-97.t: And His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿قَوْمًا لُدًّا﴾: plural of "ألَدُّ", like "أصَمُّ" and "صُمٌّ" (deaf). "اَلْألَدُّ" is the one fierce in disputation.

zajjaj:98-98.t:
And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿هَلْ تُحِسُّ مِنهم مِن أحَدٍ﴾: one says "هَلْ أحْسَسْتَ صاحِبَكَ؟", that is: "Have you seen your companion?" And you say "قَدْ حَسَّهُمْ", without alif, when he has killed them.
And His saying: ﴿أوْ تَسْمَعُ لَهم رِكْزًا﴾: "اَلرِّكْزُ" is the faint sound.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat Maryam
Meccan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿كهيعص﴾: there are three ways of reading it: with fatḥa on the hāʾ and the yāʾ, with kasra on both, and al-Ḥasan read it with ḍamma on the hāʾ: "كهُيعص", which is the least common of the dialectal forms. As for the fatḥa, it is the original; you say "ها با تا" for the letters of the alphabet. Some Arabs say "هِا يِا" with kasra [i.e. with imāla], and some of them incline towards ḍamma, saying "هُا يُا", giving a tinge of ḍamma (ishmām).
Al-Khalīl and Sībawayh reported that some Arabs say "اَلصَّلُوةُ" for "اَلصَّلاةُ", inclining towards ḍamma. As for whoever transmitted ḍamma on the hāʾ together with the yāʾ, that is anomalous (shādhdh), because the transmitters from al-Ḥasan agree on ḍamma on the hāʾ alone; ḍamma on the yāʾ is rare in the transmission from him.
There is disagreement about the explanation of "كهيعص". Most lexicographers said: they are letters of the alphabet indicating the beginning of the sūra, like "الـم" and "الـر". It was also said that their interpretation is that they are letters, each of which indicates one of the attributes of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "كافْ" indicates "كَرِيمٌ" (Generous), "ها" indicates "هادٍ" (Guide), "يا" is from "حَكِيمٌ" (Wise), "عَيْنْ" indicates "عالِمٌ" (Knowing), and "صادْ" indicates "صادِقٌ" (Truthful). This is the best that has come concerning these letters, and we have treated it exhaustively at the beginning of Sūrat al-Baqara.
And "اَلْعَيْنُ", they said, indicates "عَلِيمٌ" (All-Knowing). It is related that "كهيعص" is one of the names of Allah the Exalted, and it is related that ʿAlī — may Allah be pleased with him — swore by "كهيعص", or said: "يا كهيعص" (O Kāf-Hā-Yā-ʿAyn-Ṣād). The supplication does not indicate that it is a single name, because when the supplicant knows that supplicating with these letters indicates the attributes of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, and supplicates with them, it is as though he said: "O Sufficer (يا كافِي), O Guide, O Knower, O Truthful One." [Translator's note: here "كاف" is glossed as "كافِي" (Sufficer), whereas above it was said to indicate "كَرِيم".] So it is as though he supplicated by "كهيعص" because it is mentioned in the Qur'an and indicates these attributes. And when he swore, saying "وَكهيعص", it is as though he said: "By the Sufficer, the Guide, the Knower, the Wise and the Truthful." These letters are made quiescent because they are letters of the alphabet, in which pause is intended.

zajjaj:2-2.t:
