﴿ذِكْرُ رَحْمَتِ رَبِّكَ عَبْدَهُ زَكَرِيّا﴾: "ذِكْرُ" is nominative through something implied (muḍmar); the meaning is: "This which We recite to you is the mention of your Lord's mercy to His servant, with mercy", because the Merciful's remembering him can only be by Allah, Mighty and Majestic; and the meaning is: "your Lord's remembering His servant with mercy." "زَكَرِيّا" is read in two ways: with the short [final alif] and with the long [i.e. with hamza].
So Allah, Majestic and Mighty, made known on the tongue of His Prophet — upon him be peace — the account of Zakariyyā and Yaḥyā, so that the People of the Book would know that Muḥammad — upon him be peace — had received revelation and had been sent down to him the mention of the prophets who had passed, and that they find that in their books as he ﷺ mentioned it, while he had not recited any book nor written one with his right hand, and that he did not know that except from Allah the Exalted. His reporting of this and the like in this way was a proof of his prophethood ﷺ.
Some lexicographers said that His saying ﴿ذِكْرُ رَحْمَتِ رَبِّكَ عَبْدَهُ زَكَرِيّا﴾ is nominative through "كهيعص"; but this is impossible, because "كهيعص" is not part of what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, informed us about Zakariyyā. He has made clear in the sūra what He did for him and the good news He gave him, and nothing has come in any exegesis that "كهيعص" is the story of Zakariyyā or of Yaḥyā or any part of it. Both the one who held this view and others agree that its being nominative through an implied [element] is the correct analysis.

zajjaj:3-3.t: ﴿إذْ نادى رَبَّهُ نِداءً خَفِيًّا﴾: he called upon Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in secret.

zajjaj:4-4.t: And He made clear what he asked of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, saying: ﴿قالَ رَبِّ إنِّي وهَنَ العَظْمُ مِنِّي﴾; the meaning of "وَهَنَ" is: became weak. ﴿واشْتَعَلَ الرَّأْسُ شَيْبًا﴾: it was said that at that time he had reached sixty-five years; and it was said sixty years; and it was said seventy-five years. "شَيْبًا" is accusative as a tamyīz (specification); the meaning is: "the head blazed with grey hair." When grey hair becomes very abundant, one says: "قَدِ اشْتَعَلَ رَأْسُ فُلانٍ" (so-and-so's head has blazed). ﴿وَلَمْ أكُنْ بِدُعائِكَ رَبِّ شَقِيًّا﴾, that is: I have been one whose prayers are answered. It is also possible that he meant: "لَمْ أكُنْ بِدُعائِكَ رَبِّ شَقِيًّا", that is: "Whoever calls upon You sincerely has affirmed Your oneness and worshipped You, so I have not been wretched in worshipping You."

zajjaj:5-5.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَإنِّي خِفْتُ المَوالِيَ مِن ورائِي﴾, with the yāʾ of "مِن ورائِي" quiescent, means: after me. The singular of "اَلْمَوالِي" is "مَوْلًى"; they are the paternal cousins and a man's agnatic kin (ʿaṣaba). Its meaning is: those who come next to him in lineage, just as the meaning of "اَلْقَرابَةُ" (kinsfolk) is: those who are near to him in lineage.
His saying: ﴿فَهَبْ لِي مِن لَدُنْكَ ولِيًّا﴾, that is: I have reached this age, ﴿وامْرَأتِي عاقِرٌ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 40]. "اَلْعاقِرُ" among women is one who has a defect preventing childbirth, and likewise "اَلْعاقِرُ" among men. So I will not have a child except as an heir (وَلِيًّا) [granted by You], so grant him to me, for You have power over all things.

zajjaj:6-6.t:
His saying: ﴿يَرِثُنِي ويَرِثُ مِن آلِ يَعْقُوبَ﴾ is also read in the jussive: "يَرِثْنِي ويَرِثْ مِن آلِ يَعْقُوبَ", as the apodosis (jawāb) of the imperative. Whoever reads "يَرِثُنِي ويَرِثُ" [in the indicative] makes it a description (ṣifa) of "الوَلِيّ". It was said: "He will inherit my wealth from me, and will inherit prophethood from the family of Jacob." Some people said: it is not possible for Zakariyyā to say that he feared that his wealth would be inherited, because the way of the prophets and the righteous is that they do not fear that their relatives will inherit from them what Allah has given them; and it has come from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: «"We, the community of prophets, are not inherited from; what we leave is charity."» So they said: its meaning is: "He will inherit from me, and will inherit prophethood from the family of Jacob."
His saying: ﴿واجْعَلْهُ رَبِّ رَضِيًّا﴾, and also his saying ﴿وَلِيًّا﴾ [Maryam: 5], indicate that he asked for a religious child, because one who is not religious would not be an heir (walī) to the Prophet — upon him be peace.

zajjaj:7-7.t: His saying: ﴿إنّا نُبَشِّرُكَ﴾, and "نَبْشُرُكَ", ﴿بِغُلامٍ اسْمُهُ يَحْيى لَمْ نَجْعَلْ لَهُ مِن قَبْلُ سَمِيًّا﴾, that is: no one before him had been named "يَحْيى" (Yaḥyā); so said Ibn ʿAbbās. It was also said: "He was named 'يَحْيى' because he was made alive (ḥayiya) by the knowledge and wisdom he was given." And it was said: "لَمْ نَجْعَلْ لَهُ مِن قَبْلُ سَمِيًّا", that is: "an equal" and "a like". All of this has come in exegesis.

zajjaj:8-8.t:
His saying: ﴿قالَ رَبِّ أنّى يَكُونُ لِي غُلامٌ وكانَتِ امْرَأتِي عاقِرًا وقَدْ بَلَغْتُ مِنَ الكِبَرِ عِتِيًّا﴾ is also read "عُتِيًّا". "عُسِيًّا" with sīn has also been transmitted, but it is not permissible in recitation because it contradicts the codex (muṣḥaf). Everything that has reached its end has "عَتا يَعْتُو عِتِيًّا وعُتُوًّا وعُسُوًّا وعُسِيًّا".
So he wished to know from which direction he would have a child, when the like of his wife does not give birth and the like of him does not have children born to him.

zajjaj:9-9.t:
﴿قالَ كَذَلِكَ قالَ رَبُّكَ﴾ means — and Allah knows best —: the matter is as you have been told.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَقَدْ خَلَقْتُكَ مِن قَبْلُ ولَمْ تَكُ شَيْئًا﴾ means: "and you were not an existing thing", that is: "I brought you into existence after you had not been." That is: creating a child for you is like the creation of Adam — upon him be peace — and like your creation from a drop of fluid, a clinging clot, a lump of flesh, flesh and bone.

zajjaj:10-10.t: ﴿قالَ رَبِّ اجْعَلْ لِي آيَةً﴾, that is: a sign by which I may know that what I have been given good news of has come about. ﴿قالَ آيَتُكَ ألا تُكَلِّمَ النّاسَ ثَلاثَ لَيالٍ سَوِيًّا﴾, that is: you will be prevented from speaking while being sound, and by that you will know that Allah, Majestic and Exalted, has granted you the child. "سَوِيًّا" is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

zajjaj:11-11.t: ﴿فَخَرَجَ عَلى قَوْمِهِ مِنَ المِحْرابِ فَأوْحى إلَيْهِمْ أنْ سَبِّحُوا بُكْرَةً وعَشِيًّا﴾: it was said that the meaning of "أوْحى إلَيْهِمْ" is: he gestured to them and made signs; and it was said: he wrote for them on the ground with his hand. "بُكْرَةً وعَشِيًّا" are both accusative as [adverbs of] time.

zajjaj:12-12.t:
His saying: ﴿يا يَحْيى خُذِ الكِتابَ بِقُوَّةٍ﴾: the meaning is: "So We granted him Yaḥyā and said to him: ﴿يا يَحْيى خُذِ الكِتابَ بِقُوَّةٍ﴾", that is: with earnestness and with help from Allah, Majestic and Mighty. ﴿وَآتَيْناهُ الحُكْمَ صَبِيًّا﴾ ﴿وَحَنانًا مِن لَدُنّا وزَكاةً﴾ [Maryam: 13], that is: "and We gave him ḥanān"; "اَلْحَنانُ" is affection and mercy. The poet said:
؎فَقالَتْ حَنانٌ ما أتى بِكَ هَهُنا أذُو نَسَبٍ أمْ أنْتَ بِالحَيِّ عارِفُ
(She said: "Mercy! What brings you here? Are you a kinsman, or do you know the tribe?")
That is: "Our response is mercy," or affection and compassion. And he also said:
؎أبا مُنْذِرٍ أفْنَيْتَ فاسْتَبْقِ بَعْضَنا ∗∗∗ حَنانَيْكَ بَعْضُ الشَّرِّ أهْوَنُ مِن بَعْضِ
(Abū Mundhir, you have annihilated [us], so spare some of us — mercy upon mercy! Some evil is lighter than other evil.)
The meaning is: "And We gave him tenderness from Us and purity (zakāt)"; "اَلزَّكاةُ" is purification.
